chapters.title: Tsirutsaydan and His Idols
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 1

1There was a man whose name was Tsirutsaydan, a lover of evil, who boasted in the great number of his horses and in the strength of the army under his hand.

2He had many gods, idols, that he bowed down to and served, and he sacrificed to them day and night.

3In the folly of his heart he thought that they were the ones who gave him power and strength.

4He reckoned in his heart that they gave him authority over all his kingdom.

5He thought too that they gave him authority in war, and everything he desired.

6He himself sacrificed day and night.

7He appointed priests for the gods.

8The priests deceived him, and told him that his gods ate day and night; but they themselves ate of that unclean sacrifice.

9They also compelled others like themselves to sacrifice and eat; and they themselves sacrificed again, and compelled others to sacrifice in the same way.

10He trusted in his idol, which was of no use.

11In the blindness of his heart and the smallness of his understanding he thought that they had created him, as they fed him and made him king. For Satan had blinded his heart, so that neither he nor his people would know the God who created him, made him and established him when he did not exist, so that Satan might take him with him into punishment, and they would be punished with him forever, with those he called gods, though they were not gods.

12They ought to be called dead, for they have never been alive.

13As for the sons of men who trust in them, whose hearts are ashes: the spirit of Satan who leads them astray enters into the idol with them, and speaks to them as their hearts desire, and appears to them as they wish.

14When they see that he has done for them what they had in mind, they marvel, and they too do his will, until they slaughter their sons and their daughters who came from their own wombs, and pour out innocent blood, the blood of their sons and their daughters.

15It does not trouble them, for Satan has made it sweet to them, as their evil will wanted, to bring them down with him into his own punishment, into Gehenna, from which there is no way out, forever and ever.

16This Tsirutsaydan was proud, and he had gods: fifty in the likeness of men, and twenty in the likeness of women.

17He boasted in those gods of his, which were of no use, and he honored them greatly, and sacrificed to them evening and morning.

18He compelled people to sacrifice, and he himself ate of that unclean sacrifice, and compelled others to eat; and above all he schemed for evil.

19He made five houses for his gods, which were hammered out of bronze and iron and lead.

20He overlaid them with gold and silver, and made curtains and tents all around his house.

21He appointed keepers there, and offered to them forty fattened beasts, the sacrifices he made continually to his gods.

22He thought that his gods ate; and he set before them fifty bowls of wine, and fifty silver dishes of fine flour made with oil.

23He said to his priests, "Take it and give it to them. Let my gods eat of what I have slaughtered, and drink of all my bowls; and if it is not enough for them, I will add more."

24He compelled everyone to eat and drink of that unclean sacrifice.

25In his evil cunning he sent his soldiers to search through all his kingdom, to find out whether there was anyone who did not sacrifice or bow down to the gods, and to bring him and punish him before the king with the sword and with fire, and plunder his goods, and burn his house with fire, and take everything he had.

26"I will show him torment and punishment if he refuses to worship my gods and sacrifice to them. For they are great and kind, and in their kindness they made us.

27They made heaven and earth and the great sea, the sun and the moon and the stars, the winds and the rains, and everything that moves, for our food and to fill us.

28Those who do not worship them will be punished with pain and distress, and the gods will have no mercy on them."

Notes

  • The text — the Ge'ez of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo printed Bible, and the verse numbers follow it. No other ancient text of the book is known: no Hebrew, Greek or Latin. It is not the Greek 1 Maccabees. Its name, Maqābəyān, comes from Maccabeus (2:1), but its story and its people are its own.

  • v1 "Tsirutsaydan" — Ṣiruṣāydān, a king known only from this book. The chapter never says which land he rules; his soldiers' fame reaches all the land of Moab and the Chaldeans (2:10).

  • v8 "his gods ate" — the priests' trick is the one in the Greek story of Bel (Daniel 14 in the Greek Daniel): the priests of Bel came in through secret doors and ate up everything that had been set before Bel (14:15).

  • v11 "when he did not exist" — ʾəmḫaba ʾi-hallawo, literally "from where he was not": God made him out of nothing. The king thinks the idols made him; the verse answers that he did not exist until God made him.

  • v13 "whose hearts are ashes" — ḥamad ləbbomu. Isaiah 44:20 says the same of the man who bows down to a block of wood: He feeds on ashes; a deceived heart has led him astray. The idol itself is empty (v12, never alive); what speaks through it is Satan's spirit.

  • v14 "innocent blood, the blood of their sons and their daughters" — the words of Psalm 106:37–38 on Israel in Canaan: They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons, and poured out innocent blood, the blood of their sons and their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan.

  • vv16, 21, 22 the numbers — the Ge'ez numerals here are damaged: v16 has a stray mark for fifty and 2 for twenty; v21 has 4 for forty; v22 has stray marks for both fifties. The numbers in the verses are the ones the Ethiopian Church reads. v21 "fattened beasts" — ṣabḥāt; the verse is short here, and the word is taken as the fattened animals of the sacrifice.

  • vv26–28 — the king's speech begins with no he said; his soldiers carry it to anyone who will not sacrifice. v27 gives the idols the works of Genesis 1, sun, moon and stars, sea and everything that moves (Genesis 1:21, 9:3), and makes them all for his own table. v15 "into his own punishment" — the Ge'ez adds a word, raʾay, that does not fit the sentence and is left out.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Sons of Maccabeus
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 2

Maccabeus and His Sons

1There was a man of the tribe of Benjamin whose name was Maccabeus.

2He had [words lost]

3They found them and said to them, "Will you not bow down and sacrifice to the gods of Tsirutsaydan the king, as he commanded?

4If you refuse, we will seize you and take you to the king, and we will destroy all your goods, as the king commanded."

5These fine young men answered them, "As for us, there is One we bow down to: the God of our fathers, Creator of the heavens and the earth and the sea and all that is in it, Creator of the sun and moon and stars and clouds. He is the true God, the One we serve and believe in."

6These servants of the king were four commanders, each with fifty soldiers who carried their weapons of war.

7When they tried to seize these holy men, they escaped from their hands, and no one harmed them. They went away carrying their weapons, for they were very strong and mighty young men.

8One of them could kill a bear by strangling it, and he would strangle it at once, as one strangles a hen.

9One of them could kill a lion with a single blow of a stone or a single stroke of a club.

10One of them could kill a hundred in battle at once with one sword. So their name and their hunting were spoken of in all the land of Moab and of the Chaldeans.

11They were strong in might, and they had beauty, grace and good speech.

12The beauty of their appearance was wonderful, but above all the beauty of their hearts surpassed it, because they worshiped God and did not fear death.

The Brothers on the Mountain

13When they frightened the soldiers, no one could seize them, and being strong, they escaped to a high mountain.

14The soldiers went back into the city, shut the city gates, and terrified the people, saying, "If you do not bring us these men, the Maccabees, we will burn your city with fire, and send to the king and destroy your city."

15At that time the people of the city came out, the poor and the rich, men, widows and orphans, and all cried out together. They lifted their eyes to the mountain and cried out to them, "Do not destroy us and our city."

16Then the brothers wept together, and they feared God.

17They turned their faces toward the east, spread out their hands, and prayed to God together, saying, "Shall we refuse these men, O Lord, these who transgress Your law and Your commandment?

18We do not want to hear the word of that wicked man, who does not believe in Your law but in gold and silver, wood and stone, the work of men's hands.

19He holds that these things created him, though You are his Creator, You who kill and make alive. He sheds human blood and eats human flesh.

20We do not want to see the face of that wicked man or to hear his word.

21But if You command us, we will go to him and hand ourselves over to death for Your sake, and we will not hear the word of that wicked man when he says, 'Sacrifice to my gods.'

22We, O Lord, have trusted in You with all our heart, the God of our fathers, who did Your will and walked in Your law, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who tests the heart and the kidneys,

23who examines the righteous and the sinner and searches what is in the heart of man. Nothing is hidden from You; what is secret is uncovered before You.

24We have no other god but You.

25But be our strength and might and refuge in this work by which we serve You, so that we may hand ourselves over to death for Your holy name.

26When Israel went into the land of Egypt, You heard the prayer of Jacob; and now we ask You, holy God."

The Two Men

27When two men appeared to them and stood before them, beautiful to look at, swords of fire like lightning came down on them and killed them at once and cut off their heads; and at once they rose alive, as before.

28The beauty of their appearance became greater still. They shone more than the sun and were more beautiful than before.

Notes

  • v1 "Maccabeus" — Maqābyos, the man the book is named from (1:1 note). He is of Benjamin, and is not Judas Maccabeus of the Greek 1 Maccabees.

  • v2 "He had [words lost]" — the Ge'ez breaks off after wa-bottu, and he had. Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905) go on with three sons, the young men of v5, whose names are given at 3:1.

  • v6 "fifty soldiers" — the numeral is lost in the Ge'ez, which has wa-baba%, each with %. The number in the verse is the one the Ethiopian Church reads.

  • vv8–9 the bear and the lion — David told Saul, your servant has struck down both lions and bears (1 Samuel 17:36), and Samson tore the lion as one tears a young goat (Judges 14:6).

  • v12 "the beauty of their hearts surpassed it" — the book sets their bodily beauty (v11) against the beauty of the heart; the words for both are sən. The Lord said to Samuel, man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart (1 Samuel 16:7).

  • v19 "You who kill and make alive" — za-təqatəl wa-taḥayyu, the words of the song of Moses, I kill and I make alive (Deuteronomy 32:39), and of Hannah, The LORD kills and makes alive (1 Samuel 2:6).

  • v22 "who tests the heart and the kidneys" — ləbba wa-kwəlyāta, the words of Jeremiah, O LORD of hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the kidneys and the heart (Jeremiah 11:20; Psalm 7:9).

  • v26 "You heard the prayer of Jacob" — Genesis tells of God speaking to Jacob as he went down to Egypt, Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt (Genesis 46:3). The prayer it gives him is earlier, before he met Esau (32:9–12).

  • v27 "When two men appeared to them… and at once they rose alive" — the EOTC Ge'ez breaks off after wa-soba ʾastarʾayəwwomu, when they appeared to them; the rest of the verse is from Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905). Who was struck is said at 3:1: these who died and rose before you, the two men.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0; v27 completed from J. Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905). English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Martyrdom of Abya, Sila and Fentos
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 3

The Voice from Heaven

1A voice came from heaven saying, "Abya, Sila and Fentos, servants of God Most High: as you have seen these who died and rose before you, so you will rise after your death, and your faces will shine in the kingdom of heaven."

2They went with those men and became witnesses there.

3Then they prayed and gave thanks and bowed down to God, and death and the king's punishment did not frighten them.

Before the King

4They went to the king's servants, and did not frighten them, but were like a lamb without evil. When they reached them, the servants seized them, beat them, bound them and flogged them, and brought them to the king and stood them before him.

5The king said to them, "You rebels, how is it that you will not sacrifice and bow down to my gods?"

6Those holy, blessed, chosen and joyful brothers, Abya, Sila and Fentos, precious as a gem of great price, answered him as with one mouth.

7They said to that plague of a king, "We will not sacrifice or bow down to unclean gods that have no heart or understanding,

8or to gold and silver, wood and stone, the work of the hands of the sons of men, the work of human hands, that have no soul, mind or understanding, that do no good to the one who does them good, and no harm to the one who does them harm."

9The king answered them, "Why do you act like this and revile my honored gods? They too know who wrongs them and reviles them."

10They answered him, "We revile them and do not honor them, for they are as nothing to us."

11The king answered them, "According to the evil of your deeds I will punish you, and I will destroy the beauty of your appearance with great affliction, with flogging and with fire.

12Now tell me whether you will sacrifice to my gods or not; if not, I will raise against you the scourge, the lash, the rope and the sword."

13They answered him, "We will not bow down or sacrifice to unclean gods." The king ordered them beaten with thick rods, then with whips, and after that torn until their inner parts could be seen.

14Then they bound them and kept them in the prison, in the guardhouse, until he could decide how to kill and punish them.

15They took them to the prison and bound them with heavy chains without mercy, and they stayed in the prison three days and three nights.

The Second Trial

16After three days the king ordered a herald to go round, so that the princes, counselors, governors and elders of the city would gather.

17When King Tsirutsaydan had sat down in the court, he ordered those blessed men, Abya, Sila and Fentos, to be brought, and they stood before him, bound and wounded.

18The king said to them, "Have you chosen better while you sat these three days, or are you still in your former wickedness?"

19The blessed soldiers of God answered him, "We are steadfast, and we will not say yes to the blasphemy you speak, full of evil and uncleanness."

20That wicked man raged and ordered them hung up and their wounds opened again, and their blood flowed on the ground.

21Again he ordered them burned with torches of thorn, so that their flesh was scorched, and they did so. The blessed men said to him, "Speak on, vile one. The more you increase our punishment, the more our reward increases."

The Beasts

22Again he ordered fierce beasts brought, leopard, bear and lion, kept from their food, to be let loose on them, to finish them off at once, bones and all.

23He ordered the keepers of the beasts to let them loose on them, and they did as he commanded. They bound the holy martyrs with their hands behind them, and bound them again to stakes they had driven into the ground.

24The beasts rushed at them roaring, but when they reached the martyrs they bowed down to them and greeted them.

25They turned back roaring on their keepers, frightened the keepers and drove them on until they had brought them before the king's face.

26There they killed seventy-five of the wicked company.

27Many were crushed as they pressed on one another in fear, until the king himself left his throne and fled. With difficulty they caught the beasts and took them back to their dens.

Five Brothers

28Then there came [words lost]

29The martyrs answered their brothers, "It is not right for us to flee after we have stood up to bear witness. If you are afraid, go, flee yourselves."

30Their younger brothers said, "We too will stand with you before the king, and if you die, we will die with you."

31After this the king saw from the upper room of his royal palace that those blessed men had been set free, and that the five brothers were standing together. It was found out that the men who commanded the soldiers were their brothers, and they told the king. The king raged and roared like a wild boar in his fury.

32The king ordered the five brothers seized and put in prison until he could decide how to punish them. They took them to the prison and bound them with heavy chains in hollowed stocks, without mercy.

33King Tsirutsaydan said, "These misguided young men have worn me out. How hard the hearts of these men are! The evil of their deeds is as great as the strength of their might; when I say they will turn for the better, they make their hearts worse.

34I will repay them according to the evil of their deeds. I will burn their bodies with fire until they are ashes, and there I will scatter the ashes of their bodies like dust on a great mountain, for the wind to carry away."

The Furnace

35After he had said this, he waited three days, and then ordered the holy men brought. When the holy men came near, he ordered a fire kindled in a furnace in a great pit, and things thrown into it to make the cauldrons boil and the fire blaze: pitch and papyrus, fat, maʿāra gerā, ʾaflāṭis and sulfur.

36When the furnace was blazing, his servants went to the king and said, "We have done what you commanded. Send the men who are to be thrown in."

37He ordered them to take the men and carry them into the furnace of fire, and they did as the king commanded. When the blessed men went into it, they gave up their souls to God.

38Angels received them while those who had thrown them in looked on, and carried their souls to the bosom of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, into the garden of joy.

Notes

  • v1 "Abya, Sila and Fentos" — ʾAbyā, Silā, Fantos, the sons of Maccabeus (2:2), named here for the first time. These who died and rose before you are the two men of 2:27.

  • v2 "They went with those men and became witnesses there" — ḥoru… wa-konu samāʿta, past verbs: the verse tells it as done, and vv3–4 then tell how. Samāʿt is witnesses, the word the Church uses for its martyrs.

  • v8 "that do no good… and no harm" — Jeremiah on the idols: Do not be afraid of them, for they cannot do evil, neither is it in them to do good (Jeremiah 10:5).

  • vv22–24 the beasts bowed down to them — Daniel in the den: My God sent His messenger and shut the lions' mouths (Daniel 6:22).

  • v26 "seventy-five" — the Ge'ez has wa-5, and five; the tens are lost. The number in the verse is the one the Ethiopian Church reads.

  • v28 "Then there came [words lost]" — the Ge'ez has only wa-maṣʾu, and they came. Vv29–31 show what is missing: two younger brothers come to the three.

  • v31 "that the five brothers were standing together… in his fury" — the EOTC Ge'ez breaks off after wa-yəqawwəmu, and they were standing; the rest of the verse is from Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905).

  • v35 "a furnace… pitch and papyrus" — the furnace of Daniel 3, heated seven times more than it was usually heated (Daniel 3:19); in the Greek of Daniel the servants fed it with naphtha, pitch, tow and brushwood (3:46). Maʿāra gerā and ʾaflāṭis are two more burning materials whose names are not otherwise known.

  • v38 "the bosom of Abraham" — ḥəḍna ʾAbrəhām, where the angels carried Lazarus (Luke 16:22).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0; v31 completed from J. Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905). English translation by this project.

He ordered the keepers of the beasts to let them loose on them, and they did as he commanded. They bound the holy martyrs with their hands behind them, and bound them again to stakes they had driven into the ground.
The beasts rushed at them roaring, but when they reached the martyrs they bowed down to them and greeted them.
They turned back roaring on their keepers, frightened the keepers and drove them on until they had brought them before the king's face.
There they killed seventy-five of the wicked company.
Many were crushed as they pressed on one another in fear, until the king himself left his throne and fled. With difficulty they caught the beasts and took them back to their dens.
Five Brothers
Then there came [words lost]
The martyrs answered their brothers, "It is not right for us to flee after we have stood up to bear witness. If you are afraid, go, flee yourselves."
Their younger brothers said, "We too will stand with you before the king, and if you die, we will die with you."

After this the king saw from the upper room of his royal palace that those blessed men had been set free, and that the five brothers were standing together. It was found out that the men who commanded the soldiers were their brothers, and they told the king. The king raged and roared like a wild boar in his fury.

King Tsirutsaydan said, "These misguided young men have worn me out. How hard the hearts of these men are! The evil of their deeds is as great as the strength of their might; when I say they will turn for the better, they make their hearts worse.

chapters.title: The Martyrs Appear to the King
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 4

Fire, Sea and Beasts

1When that wicked man saw that they were dead, he ordered their bodies burned with fire until they became like dust, to be scattered by the wind. But the fire could not burn the hair of their heads from their bodies, and they brought them out of the pit.

2Again they kindled fire over them from morning until evening, and it did not touch them. Again he said, "Come, let us throw their bodies into the sea."

3They did as the king commanded and threw them into the sea. Yet the sea did not swallow them, though they had loaded them with heavy irons, great stones and millstones turned by donkeys. They did not sink into the sea but floated on the surface of the deep, for the Spirit of God was on them; and in everything he schemed against them, he failed.

4He said, "Since these bodies of theirs have worn me out more than their lives did, what shall I do? I will throw their bodies to the beasts to eat."

5They did so, and the beasts and the birds did not touch their bodies. Their bodies lay there fourteen days, while eagles and birds shaded them with their wings from the heat of the sun, the bodies of the five martyrs.

6When people saw them, their bodies shone like the rays of the sun, and angels surrounded their bodies like a tent of light.

7He took counsel and found nothing he could do, and after that he dug the ground and buried the bodies of the five martyrs.

The Five in the Night

8The five martyrs appeared at night to that wicked king while he was sleeping on his bed, and stood before him holding their swords.

9When he woke he was afraid and wanted to flee from corner to corner of the house, for it seemed to him that men had come into his house to do him wrong. His knees shook and he was afraid, for it seemed to him that they would kill him.

10So he said, "What do you want, my lords? What shall I do for you?"

11They answered him, "Are we not the ones you killed and burned, and ordered thrown into the sea? But you failed, for God kept our bodies, because we trusted in Him. Glory to God! For whoever trusts in Him does not perish, and we who trusted in Him have not been put to shame."

12He said to them, "What reward shall I give you in return for the evil I did to you? For I did not know that such punishment would come upon me.

13Now set out for me the reward I am to give you, so that you do not take my life in death or bring me down alive to Sheol.

14For I have sinned. Forgive me this wrong of mine, for the law of your Father is mercy."

15The blessed martyrs answered him, "We will not repay you evil for the evil you did to us. The Lord our God is the One who will repay you, for repayment belongs to God.

16But we have appeared to you as living, because of the blindness of your heart and the smallness of your understanding. As for us, while you thought you were killing us, you were preparing life for us.

17You and your gods will go down into the punishment of burning fire, where there is no way out forever.

18Woe to you, you and your gods that you serve and bow down to, when you have stopped bowing down to God who created you! You are spittle, and do not know where you came from. Are you not smoke that passes, seen today and gone tomorrow?"

19The king answered them, "What do you command me, so that I may do all you wish?"

20They said to him, "It is not for our own sake that we teach you, but for yours, so that you do not go into the punishment of burning fire.

21For your gods are gold and silver, wood and stone, the work of men's hands, that have no soul, mind or understanding.

22They do not kill and do not make alive, they do no good and do no harm, they do not humble and do not honor, they do not make poor and do not make rich, they do not uproot and do not plant. They lead you astray by the spirit of demons, who do not want a single man to be saved,

23above all those like you, blind of heart, who think that these created you, when it was you who made them.

24For the spirits of demons and of satans gather and answer you as you wish, to drown you in the sea of fire.

25But you, leave this error and serve the Lord our God, and let this be our reward in return for our death, so that we may gain for our souls."

26He was dismayed and astonished, and marveled and was afraid, for their swords were drawn [words lost]

27He said, "Now I know that the dead who have become ashes truly rise; as for me, I have barely escaped being killed."

28After that they vanished from the king's eyes. From that day Tsirutsaydan, proud and arrogant as he was, gave up burning their bodies.

The King's Error

29He rejoiced in the error of his heart and in his gods, for they had led him astray many days. It was not he alone who went astray; he led many like him astray, until they gave up following the One who created them.

30They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons, and did the will of their heart, the fornication and lewdness that their father Satan had taught them, to make the disorder and lewdness that God does not delight in.

31They took their mothers as wives and defiled their sisters and their kinswomen, and every deed like this, filthy deeds. They defiled their souls and refused to turn back, for Satan had hardened the hearts of those crooked men.

32That Tsirutsaydan was proud and arrogant; he did not know his Creator, and boasted in his gods.

33How does God give a kingdom to those who do not know Him? He said: because He tests them, whether they will turn and come back to Him.

34If they turn and come back to Him, He loves them and keeps their kingdom; but if they refuse, He punishes them in the trembling of Gehenna forever.

35A king is to fear the Lord God, as great as his kingdom is; and a ruler is to submit himself well to his Creator, as great as his rule is.

36The learned, the great men and the stewards are to obey their Creator, as great as their honor is.

37For He created all creation, He the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who makes poor and makes rich, who humbles and honors; for there is no other god besides Him in heaven above or on the earth below.

Notes

  • v3 "millstones turned by donkeys" — maḫrəḍa ʾadg, a donkey's millstone. Jesus' saying: it would be better for him to have a great millstone fastened around his neck and to be drowned in the depth of the sea (Matthew 18:6), where great millstone is in Greek mylos onikos, a donkey's millstone.

  • v5 "fourteen days… the bodies of the five martyrs" — the Ge'ez has 4 for the days; the tens are lost, and the number in the verse is the one the Ethiopian Church reads. The EOTC text then breaks off; the bodies of the five martyrs is from Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905).

  • v8 — the EOTC Ge'ez has only they appeared at night to that wicked king; the rest of the verse is from Horovitz's excerpts.

  • v15 "repayment belongs to God" — Vengeance is Mine, and repayment (Deuteronomy 32:35); Paul quotes it: Never avenge yourselves… for it is written, "Vengeance is Mine, I will repay, says the Lord" (Romans 12:19).

  • v18 "smoke that passes, seen today and gone tomorrow" — What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes (James 4:14).

  • v22 "They do not kill and do not make alive… do not uproot and do not plant" — what the idols cannot do is what Hannah says the LORD does: The LORD kills and makes alive… The LORD makes poor and makes rich; He brings low and He exalts (1 Samuel 2:6–7). To uproot… to build and to plant is the charge given to Jeremiah (Jeremiah 1:10).

  • v26 "for their swords were drawn [words lost]" — the Ge'ez breaks off at ʾasyəftihomu la-, their swords, of the…

  • v33 "He said" — wa-yəbe. The verse does not say whose words these are.

  • v37 "in heaven above or on the earth below" — Moses: the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath; there is no other (Deuteronomy 4:39).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0; vv5 and 8 completed from J. Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905). English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Proud Kings
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 5

Kings Brought Down

1The giant was proud, and with one gnat God made his body swell from his feet to his head, and by that small gnat he died.

2Again Nimrod was proud, who had a bed of iron made because of his great strength; God destroyed him too.

3Again Nebuchadnezzar was proud, and said, "There is no other king besides me. I am the one who makes the sun rise on the earth." Out of his great pride he said this.

4God drove him from among men for seven years, and made his portion with the beasts and the birds of the sky, until he knew that it was God who had created him.

5When he knew it, God brought him back again into his kingdom. Who has defied God his Creator and been proud against Him, and has not become dust?

6Who has transgressed His law and His ordinance, and the earth has not swallowed him?

7You too, Tsirutsaydan, want to be proud against your Creator; and you too are bound, like them, to be overthrown for your pride and brought down to the dust of death,

8and further, to Sheol, the end of darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, below, beneath, into the great and deep pit, from which there is no way out forever.

9You are a man, and dust, who will die tomorrow like the proud kings like you, who left the life of this world.

The Creator of All

10We say to you: you are a man and not God; for God is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and your Creator.

11He brings down the proud and lifts up the humble; He gives strength to the weak and weakness to the strong.

12He gives death to the living, and raises the dead who lay in the grave and became dust.

13He frees the slaves into life from the slavery of sin.

14O King Tsirutsaydan, why do you boast in your unclean gods, which are of no use?

15God made the heavens and founded the earth, created the great sea, set the sun and moon in place, and ordered the seasons and the years.

16Man goes out to his work and labors until evening, and the stars of heaven stand firm at His word.

17He counts them all by their names, and nothing happens that God does not know.

18He commanded the angels of heaven to serve Him and praise His holy name, and He sends all the angels to those who will inherit life.

19The angel Raphael was sent to Tobit, and saved Tobias in the land of Raguel.

20An angel was sent to Gideon to tell him how to destroy the foreigners, and an angel was sent to Moses the prophet when he brought Israel across the Red Sea.

21For it says: God alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.

22He made them ride on the heights of the land.

23He fed them the produce of the fields, and nursed them with honey from the rock, for He loved them greatly.

What God Asks of a King

24To you also He gave kingship over His people, and gave you authority over four kingdoms, to guard the people, to shepherd them in uprightness, and to do the will of the One who created you.

25He made you king greatly, so that you would love the Lord your God, for He raised you above all and made you king.

26You too ought to love the Lord your God greatly, as He loved you and trusted you over all His flock. Do the will of God, so that your days on the earth may be long and He may be with you,

27that He may stand for you against all your enemies, seat you on your throne, and spread His wings over your head.

28If you would know it, God chose you as He chose Saul from the sons of Israel and made him king over Israel His people, while he was tending his father's donkeys, and Saul sat on the throne with Samuel the prophet.

29God gave him a greater portion than his brothers, and said to him, "From now on God has made you king over His people. Keep His people."

30Regard those who do good with good, and those who do evil with evil, for God has set you over them to kill and to keep alive,

31to repay those who do good with good and those who do evil with evil. For God has set you over all you wish, so that you may do His will, whether you punish or let live.

32You too, do the will of God at every time and every hour, so that He may do your will in all you think of and all you ask, as you humble yourself before Him. For you too are the servant of Him who rules over all, who is above.

33No one judges Him; He judges all.

34No one appoints Him; He appoints all.

35No one overthrows Him; He overthrows all.

36No one sets Him free; He sets all free.

37No one compels Him; He compels all. No one escapes from His hand, for the judgment of heaven and earth is with Him.

38Nothing is hidden before His eyes; everything is uncovered before Him.

39He sees all, and no one sees Him. He hears the prayer of the one who prays to Him and accepts his prayer, for He created man in His image and in His likeness.

40He feeds all from His storehouse, which never runs short, for He is the King who lives forever.

Notes

  • v1 "The giant… with one gnat" — raʿāytāwi, the giant, from raʿāyt, the word for the giants of 1 Enoch (they bore great giants, 1 Enoch 7:2) and of this book (18:2). Which giant is not said. Fəṣṣənt is taken as gnat. Nimrod, in the next verse, is a giant on the earth in the Greek of Genesis 10:8.

  • v2 "a bed of iron" — in the Bible the bed of iron is Og's: his bed was a bed of iron (Deuteronomy 3:11). Nimrod is a mighty hunter before the LORD (Genesis 10:8–9).

  • vv3–5 Nebuchadnezzar — You shall be driven from among men, and your dwelling shall be with the beasts of the field… and seven periods of time shall pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules the kingdom of men (Daniel 4:32). His reason returned and his kingdom was given back (4:36).

  • v6 "and the earth has not swallowed him" — Korah and his company: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up (Numbers 16:32).

  • vv7–10 the speaker — the chapter speaks to the king without naming who speaks: We say to you (v10). It goes on to the end of the chapter. v10 "you are a man and not God" — the word to the prince of Tyre: you are a man, and not God (Ezekiel 28:2).

  • v18 "He sends all the angels to those who will inherit life" — Are they not all ministering spirits sent out to serve for the sake of those who are to inherit salvation? (Hebrews 1:14).

  • v20 "to destroy the foreigners" — ʾIloflí, from the Greek allophyloi, foreigners, the Greek Bible's word for the Philistines. In Judges, Gideon's enemy is Midian (Judges 6:11–16). The angel at the sea is the one of Exodus 14:19.

  • vv21–23 — the song of Moses: the LORD alone led him, and there was no foreign god with him. He made him ride on the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field, and He made him suck honey from the rock (Deuteronomy 32:12–13).

  • v36 "No one sets Him free; He sets all free" — yəgʿəzo… yəgʿəz, the verb of v13, He frees the slaves.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Dwellings of the Kings
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 6

The Dwelling of the Good Kings

1The kings wrote of Him what is right, for He makes the kings who do His will reign in righteousness.

2He makes their dwelling shine with a light that cannot be told, where Abraham, Isaac and Jacob are, David and Solomon and Ezekiel, and all the good kings whose dwelling is bright, for they did the will of God. It is not like a hall on earth, but a hall in heaven, very awesome, and its floor is pure, the color of gold and silver and jacinth.

3Its appearance is very bright, beyond the thought of man: the hall of the kingdom of heaven, shining with topaz and emerald, ṭalmā and warāwər,

4and with every precious stone beyond the thought of man. The hall of the kingdom is very bright, which He Himself, the Craftsman, made as He knows: the hall of the kingdom of heaven. Its floor is pure, the color of gold and silver and jacinth, green and yellow, the color of jacinth and fine silk.

5So it is very beautiful and lovely, pure and bright,

6woven with righteousness and uprightness, and built with kindness and mercy.

7Water of life flows there, very pure, like the sun, and there is a tent of light, ringed with the ʾakwāl of Hermon.

8Around its house are planted the sweet fruits of the garden, each with its own look and fragrance, and a vineyard, olive trees and oil, very good, and the fragrance of its fruit is sweet.

9If one of flesh went in there, his soul would go out of him at the sweetness of the fragrance of its fruit, for the greatness of the joy that is there.

10There the good kings who did the will of God rejoice. Their deeds and their station are known, in the place of life forever, in the kingdom of heaven.

11He has shown that it is on earth as it is in heaven: as great as their kingdom on earth is, and as people honor them and bow down to them, so in heaven they are honored and exalted and rejoice, if they did good in their life on the earth.

The Dwelling of the Harsh Kings

12But the kings who are harsh in their kingdom and in the rule God gave them, who do not judge with righteousness and uprightness, and do not save the oppressed, the guest and the orphan, for they have ignored the voice of the poor and the needy,

13who do not save the poor and the needy from the hand of the one who robs them, do not fill the hungry from their food or give the thirsty drink from their drink, and have not turned their ears to the cry of the sons of men,

16But in heaven is the One who holds all. The souls of all are in His hand, and the life of all is in His mouth. He gives honor to those who honor Him, and loves those who love Him, for He rules all and judges all.

17He tests the heart and the kidneys, for He is the King of heaven and earth, who grants his prayer to the one who prays to Him with a pure heart.

18He breaks the pride of the mighty who do evil to widows and orphans.

Saul and Agag

19It is not by your might that you took this kingdom, nor by your power that you sit on this throne. He Himself chose to seat you on the throne of the kingdom, to test you, whether you can rule His people, as with Saul, who in those days ruled His people and disregarded the word of God and the word of Samuel the prophet, and did not kill the king of Amalek and his men.

20For God said to Samuel the prophet, "Go, tell Saul: Go and make war on the land of Amalek, and kill all their kings and all who live there, man and beast, for they have provoked Me by transgressing the law, by serving gods and bowing down to idols in their shrines, and by every filthy deed that is of no use."

21Because of this, when they provoked God, He sent Saul to kill them.

22But he spared their king, and many cattle, and women and virgins, and the finest of the young men. Because of this God said to Samuel the prophet, "Because he has despised My word and not heard My command, go and tear his kingdom away.

23Anoint David son of Jesse to reign over Israel in his place.

24As for him, let loose on him a demon that will strangle him.

25For I gave him the kingdom so that he would do My will, and when he refused to do My will, I put him out of his honor. As for you, go, tell him, and say to him: Is this how you disregard God, who made you king over His people Israel and set you on the throne of His kingdom?

26You did not know how great the honor and greatness was that He gave you."

27Samuel the prophet went to Saul the king, and came in to him while he was at table, with Agag king of Amalek on his left.

28He said to him, "Why have you so utterly disregarded God, who commanded you to kill man and beast?"

29Then the king was afraid, rose from his seat and took hold of Samuel's garment. Samuel refused to turn back, and Samuel's garment tore.

30Samuel said to Saul, "God has torn your kingdom away."

31Again Saul said to Samuel, "Honor me before the people, and make atonement for me before God so that He may forgive me." Samuel refused to turn back from his word, for he feared the word of God his Creator and did not fear a mortal king.

32Because of this he pierced Agag king of Amalek while the food was still in his mouth.

33As for that wicked man who had despised the word of God, an evil spirit seized him and struck his head. For God is not abashed before a king who does wrong, for He is the King of kings, who commands all.

34No one commands Him, for He is the Lord of all creation, who overthrows all the authority of the kings and rulers who do not fear Him.

35From Saul too He took the kingdom away, from him and from his son, as it says: "The house of David goes on rising, and the house of Saul goes on sinking."

36God took vengeance on the seed of the house of Saul, because he had provoked Him and had not destroyed His enemies, who provoked Him with their evil deeds. For whoever does not take vengeance on God's enemy is himself God's enemy.

37Whoever does not take vengeance on the sinner, though he can and has the authority, he truly is the enemy of God, who does not punish the one who is without God's law.

chapters.title: A Word to Kings and Rulers
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 7

What Are You?

1Whether you are a king or a ruler, what are you? Is it not God who created you,

2and brought you from where you were not, so that you would do His will, walk in His commandment and fear His judgment? As you are angry with your servants and have power over them, so there is One who is angry with you and has power over you.

3As you strike without mercy those who do wrong, so there is God, who will strike you and cast you into judgment where there is no way out forever.

4As you flog the one who has not submitted to you and has not brought you a gift, why do you not bring a gift to God?

5As you want them to fear you, why do you not fear the Lord your God? For He created you and made you king over all His works, to shepherd His people and His flock in righteousness.

Judge with Righteousness

6Do not show favor to the great or the small, but judge with righteousness and uprightness, as God has appointed you. Whom do you fear besides Him? Keep His ways and His commandment.

7Do not turn aside to the right or to the left, as Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying to them, "I have set before you fire and water; stretch out your hand to whichever you wish."

8Hear the word I set before you, so that you hear His word and do His commandment, and do not say, "It is beyond the river. Who will bring it to me, so that I may see it and hear His word and do the commandment of God?"

9Or if again you say, "Who will go up for me to heaven and bring that word of God down to me, so that I may hear it and do it?", He has said, "See, the word is near you, in your mouth and in your hand."

10If you do not hear the Scripture, you do not hear the Lord your God; and if you do not keep His word, you do not love Him or do His commandment.

11You are bound to go into eternal judgment if you do not love His commandment and do not do the will of Him who exalted you and honored you above all your people, so that you would shepherd them in your righteousness.

12He set you above them, as head over all His people, so that you would remember the name of your God who created you, and He gave you the people to rule with righteousness and uprightness.

13Among those who wrong you are some you are to rebuke and some you are to pardon, as you remember the way of God, set your mind right and judge uprightly.

14When they dispute before you, do not show favor, and do not take a bribe from a man to acquit him, or to wrong an innocent man, for the whole earth is yours.

15If you do His will, He will lengthen your days.

16Remember that you will rise from the dead and stand before His face, and be examined for all you have done, whether evil or good.

17If you do good, you will dwell in the dwelling of the good kings, in the houses of light; but if you do evil, you will dwell in the dwelling of the evil kings. God is not abashed by your rank.

When You See Your Glory

18But you, when you see the greatness of your majesty, the adornment of your warriors and your weapons hung up, and look on your horses and the soldiers under your hand, and those who blow the horn and play the harp before you,

19when you see all this, you lift up your mind and stiffen your neck, and do not remember the One who gave you all this honor. When He says to you, "Let it go," will you not let it go?

20He will give your honor to another, for you have utterly disregarded the charge He gave you.

21There He will search you, call you to account and judge you. For death comes to you suddenly, and at the resurrection there will be judgment, and the deeds of men will be examined.

22For the kings of the earth there is none who honors them, and the crown the princes of the earth boast in will fall; for rich and poor stand together in judgment, for He is the righteous Judge.

The Dead Will Rise

23In the judgment that is ready, the soul trembles, the books are opened, the deeds of men are shown, and nothing is covered,

24at the resurrection of the dead. For the earth gives back what was entrusted to it, as a woman cannot hold her womb closed once she has come to childbirth and what is in her belly is ready to come out.

25Or can the clouds hold back the rain, so that they do not send it where God has commanded them and it does not come down? So it cannot be that the dead will not rise once the time of resurrection has come. For the word of God brought all things from where there was nothing, and the word of God brought all down to the depths.

26Again, the word of God will bring all up from the depths, as Moses said: "Not by bread alone does man live, but by every word that comes out of the mouth of God."

27So it is known that the dead live by the word of God.

28Again He said in Deuteronomy, concerning those who become kings and rulers and do their own will: "On the day of judgment I will take vengeance on them, in the time when their foot slips, for the day of their reckoning is near."

29Again God says to those who do not know the judgment of God: "Know, know that I am God. I kill and I make alive.

30I strike and I have mercy; I bring down to Sheol and bring up again to heaven; and there is none who escapes from My hand."

31So God has said concerning the kings and rulers who did not keep His commandment: "Keep My law and My ordinance, so that you may enter My kingdom forever; for the kingdom on earth passes away, and moves on from morning to evening."

32For the cup of God is for honor and for shame: this one He shames, and that one He honors.

33The one who does not do His will He removes, and the one who does His will He appoints.

Notes

  • v7 "I have set before you fire and water; stretch out your hand to whichever you wish" — the words are Sirach's: He has placed before you fire and water: stretch out your hand for whichever you wish (Sirach 15:16). Moses set before Israel life and death, blessing and curse (Deuteronomy 30:19).

  • vv8–9 "beyond the river… Who will go up for me to heaven" — Moses: It is not in heaven, that you should say, "Who will go up for us to heaven and bring it to us?"… Neither is it beyond the sea… But the word is very near you. It is in your mouth and in your heart (Deuteronomy 30:12–14). Here it is the river and your hand. Paul quotes the passage (Romans 10:6–8).

  • v14 "for the whole earth is yours" — ʾəsma ziʾaka yəʾəti mədr kwəllantāhā; the verse gives no more reason than that.

  • v23 "the books are opened" — Daniel: the court sat in judgment, and the books were opened (Daniel 7:10); John: the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to what they had done (Revelation 20:12).

  • v24 "the earth gives back what was entrusted to it" — 1 Enoch: In those days the earth will give back what was entrusted to it, and Sheol will give back what was entrusted to it (1 Enoch 51:1).

  • v26 "Not by bread alone does man live" — Deuteronomy 8:3, the word Jesus answered the tempter with (Matthew 4:4).

  • v28 "On the day of judgment I will take vengeance on them, in the time when their foot slips" — the song of Moses: Vengeance is Mine, and repayment, for the time when their foot slips; for the day of their calamity is near (Deuteronomy 32:35).

  • vv29–30 "I kill and I make alive. I strike and I have mercy" — See now that I, I am He… I kill and I make alive; I wound and I heal; and there is none that can deliver out of My hand (Deuteronomy 32:39). He brings down to Sheol and raises up is Hannah's (1 Samuel 2:6).

  • v32 "the cup of God… this one He shames, and that one He honors" — It is God who judges, putting down one and lifting up another. For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup (Psalm 75:7–8).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Likenesses of the Resurrection
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 8

The Tree and the Four Parts

1Hear, and I will tell you about the resurrection of the dead too. Trees are planted and put out branches, and the vine puts out tendrils, and people take their harvest from it; for God brings the fruit from where there was none.

2See: the tree you planted was small, and it comes out with branches and leaves and fruit.

3God waters its roots from two breasts, from the water and from the earth.

4Its wood He feeds from the wind and from the sun. The root gives water to the leaves, and the earth gives strength to the wood.

5The Spirit of God gives fruit among them. So too is the resurrection of the dead.

6He said, "Gather the souls from the four winds, from the water and the earth, from the sun and the wind"; for each part went to its own once the soul went out from the flesh.

7The earth stayed with its own and became ashes; the water stayed with its own and became dew;

8the wind stayed with its own and became wind; and the fire stayed with its own and became the warmth of the sun.

9The spirit returned into the hand of its Creator, and He sets it where He wishes, so that He may bring it back when He wishes.

10The souls of the righteous He keeps in the houses of light, and the souls of sinners He shuts in the houses of darkness, until the time He chooses to bring them out.

11He said to Ezekiel the prophet, "Call from the four winds, so that they may gather and become one spirit."

12When he spoke so, with one word they gathered from the four winds.

13The water brought dew, and the sun brought warmth.

14The earth brought ashes, and the wind brought breath.

15God brought the soul from its dwelling, where He had shut it. With one word they gathered, and there was resurrection.

Night and Morning

16Again I will show you a likeness that is near you. Evening comes and you sleep; morning comes and you rise. When you sleep, you are dead;

17when you wake, it is a likeness of the resurrection. The night is a likeness of this world, which is all darkness; the whole world sleeps in it, for the darkness of night has covered them.

18The dawn of morning is a likeness of the resurrection of the dead, by which the darkness is taken away and there is light in all the world, and man rises and goes out to his work.

19So it is with the renewal of the world and the resurrection of the dead; for this world passes away, as this night does.

20When the sun comes and shines, it is a likeness of this world, as David said, "In the sun He has set His tent."

21When He comes, in the new world, as the sun shines now, when God Himself comes upon it, He will shine on the new world. For He has said, "A sun that does not set and a lamp that is not quenched: God Himself is its light."

The Seed

22Again, He will raise the dead in the twinkling of an eye. Again, I will bring you a likeness from your food, which you sow and live by, whether a grain of wheat or a grain of barley or a grain of lentil, and all the work of man that is sown in all the earth: if it does not die, nothing comes to life.

23When it dies, its body is consumed in the dust with its husk, as you see a man's body.

24When its body has been consumed by the earth, it sprouts, as much as [words lost]

25See: if it did not die, it could not live; but when it has sprouted, it puts out a great crop.

26From God fruit is given to that crop that has grown, and He clothes it with body, skin and husk.

27The leaves, the straw, the chaff and the ears are not counted for you; but see how the grain of what you sowed has multiplied.

28Do not be a fool, but see how your seed has multiplied. So too think of the resurrection of the dead, and how they are repaid according to their deeds.

29Again, hear, and I will tell you how a seed does not change into another seed. If you sow wheat, do you reap barley?

30If you sow cumin, do you reap flax? Among the trees, if you plant a fig, does it come up an almond? If you plant a walnut, does it come up a vine for you?

31If you plant sweet fruit, does it come up bitter? If you plant a bitter tree, can it become sweet?

32So too, if a sinner dies, can he become righteous at the resurrection? Or if a righteous man dies, can he become a sinner at the resurrection? Each is repaid according to his deeds, according to the fruit of his work and the work of his hands, and no one is judged for the sin of another.

The Dew of Life

33The cedar of Lebanon is planted and puts out long, great branches; but if the dew of Hermon does not fall on it, its leaves do not flourish, and it dries up and is shaken off.

34The zəgbā is torn out by the roots if the winter rain does not come down on it.

35So too, if there does not come down on them [words lost] of life from God, the dead will not rise.

Notes

  • vv6, 11–15 Ezekiel and the four winds — Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live (Ezekiel 37:9). The chapter reads the valley of dry bones as the resurrection of the body: earth, water, wind and fire each give back their part (vv7–8, 13–14).

  • v9 "The spirit returned into the hand of its Creator" — the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it (Ecclesiastes 12:7).

  • v11 "become one spirit" — 1 manfas, written with the digit.

  • v20 "In the sun He has set His tent" — Psalm 19:4 in the Greek, In the sun He set His tent; the Hebrew has In them He has set a tent for the sun.

  • v21 "A sun that does not set and a lamp that is not quenched: God Himself is its light" — Your sun shall no more go down… for the LORD will be your everlasting light (Isaiah 60:20); the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light (Revelation 21:23).

  • vv22–26 the seed — Paul: What you sow does not come to life unless it dies… God gives it a body as He has chosen, and to each kind of seed its own body (1 Corinthians 15:36–38). In the twinkling of an eye is his too (15:52).

  • v24 "as much as [words lost]" — the Ge'ez breaks off at maṭana, as much as.

  • v32 "no one is judged for the sin of another" — The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not suffer for the iniquity of the father (Ezekiel 18:20).

  • vv33–35 the dew — the dew of Hermon, which falls on the mountains of Zion (Psalm 133:3). V35 breaks off where the word for what comes down should be; vv33–34 name dew and rain. Isaiah: your dew is a dew of light, and the earth will give birth to the dead (Isaiah 26:19). Zəgbā (v34) is a tree whose kind is uncertain.

speech.text: 1 Meqabyan 8
The Tree and the Four Parts

Hear, and I will tell you about the resurrection of the dead too. Trees are planted and put out branches, and the vine puts out tendrils, and people take their harvest from it; for God brings the fruit from where there was none.
See: the tree you planted was small, and it comes out with branches and leaves and fruit.
God waters its roots from two breasts, from the water and from the earth.
Its wood He feeds from the wind and from the sun. The root gives water to the leaves, and the earth gives strength to the wood.
The Spirit of God gives fruit among them. So too is the resurrection of the dead.
He said, "Gather the souls from the four winds, from the water and the earth, from the sun and the wind"; for each part went to its own once the soul went out from the flesh.
The earth stayed with its own and became ashes; the water stayed with its own and became dew;
the wind stayed with its own and became wind; and the fire stayed with its own and became the warmth of the sun.
The spirit returned into the hand of its Creator, and He sets it where He wishes, so that He may bring it back when He wishes.
The souls of the righteous He keeps in the houses of light, and the souls of sinners He shuts in the houses of darkness, until the time He chooses to bring them out.
He said to Ezekiel the prophet, "Call from the four winds, so that they may gather and become one spirit."
When he spoke so, with one word they gathered from the four winds.
The water brought dew, and the sun brought warmth.
The earth brought ashes, and the wind brought breath.
God brought the soul from its dwelling, where He had shut it. With one word they gathered, and there was resurrection.
Night and Morning
Again I will show you a likeness that is near you. Evening comes and you sleep; morning comes and you rise. When you sleep, you are dead;
when you wake, it is a likeness of the resurrection. The night is a likeness of this world, which is all darkness; the whole world sleeps in it, for the darkness of night has covered them.
The dawn of morning is a likeness of the resurrection of the dead, by which the darkness is taken away and there is light in all the world, and man rises and goes out to his work.
So it is with the renewal of the world and the resurrection of the dead; for this world passes away, as this night does.
When the sun comes and shines, it is a likeness of this world, as David said, "In the sun He has set His tent."

When He comes, in the new world, as the sun shines now, when God Himself comes upon it, He will shine on the new world. For He has said, "A sun that does not set and a lamp that is not quenched: God Himself is its light."
The Seed

Again, He will raise the dead in the twinkling of an eye. Again, I will bring you a likeness from your food, which you sow and live by, whether a grain of wheat or a grain of barley or a grain of lentil, and all the work of man that is sown in all the earth: if it does not die, nothing comes to life.
When it dies, its body is consumed in the dust with its husk, as you see a man's body.
When its body has been consumed by the earth, it sprouts, as much as [words lost]
See: if it did not die, it could not live; but when it has sprouted, it puts out a great crop.
From God fruit is given to that crop that has grown, and He clothes it with body, skin and husk.
The leaves, the straw, the chaff and the ears are not counted for you; but see how the grain of what you sowed has multiplied.
Do not be a fool, but see how your seed has multiplied. So too think of the resurrection of the dead, and how they are repaid according to their deeds.
Again, hear, and I will tell you how a seed does not change into another seed. If you sow wheat, do you reap barley?
If you sow cumin, do you reap flax? Among the trees, if you plant a fig, does it come up an almond? If you plant a walnut, does it come up a vine for you?
If you plant sweet fruit, does it come up bitter? If you plant a bitter tree, can it become sweet?

So too, if a sinner dies, can he become righteous at the resurrection? Or if a righteous man dies, can he become a sinner at the resurrection? Each is repaid according to his deeds, according to the fruit of his work and the work of his hands, and no one is judged for the sin of another.
The Dew of Life
The cedar of Lebanon is planted and puts out long, great branches; but if the dew of Hermon does not fall on it, its leaves do not flourish, and it dries up and is shaken off.
The zəgbā is torn out by the roots if the winter rain does not come down on it.
So too, if there does not come down on them [words lost] of life from God, the dead will not rise.

chapters.title: The Rain of Mercy
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 9

Without the Rain of Mercy

1The valleys of Gilboa and the mountains of Lebanon, if the rain of mercy does not come down on them from God, do not sprout grass for the cattle and the beasts.

2The mountains of Gilead and the valleys of Elam give no green grass to the goats and the flocks of rams that are seen there, or to the wild animals, the ibex, the wild oxen and the deer.

3So too the rebels and the heretics, who of old took up rebellion and error: if the dew of mercy does not come down on them from God, the dead will not rise. So too the sorcerers and the sinners, Qoṗros and Dimāso, the slanderers,

4and those who sit at divination and spells, and the murderers,

5and those who fornicate without law, and the ʾAtnāwyān and the Medes, who trust in their idols and think of them and delight in them with drum and lyre and harp,

6who act like madmen with their idols and fornicate with the work of their hands, which cannot save themselves: these will be judged on the day of judgment, at the resurrection.

The Horn of Michael

7O fool, poor of mind, do you think that the dead will not rise?

8Do not think so, for you will not sleep there when the horn is blown at the resurrection of the dead by the mouth of Michael the archangel.

9The mountains and the hills will be brought low, the rivers and the depths will be leveled, and they will become a straight road.

10There will be resurrection for all flesh.

Notes

  • v1 "The valleys of Gilboa… if the rain of mercy does not come down on them" — David's lament for Saul: You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain upon you (2 Samuel 1:21). The chapter goes on from 8:33–35, the cedar that withers without the dew of Hermon.

  • v2 "the ibex, the wild oxen and the deer" — wa-yəṭal wa-torāt wa-ḫayyālāt, three wild animals of the hills.

  • v3 "Qoṗros and Dimāso" — two names in a list of kinds of sinners. Qoṗros is the Ge'ez for Cyprus (13:3); Dimāso is not otherwise known. What the names stand for here is not said.

  • v5 "the ʾAtnāwyān" — a people named with the Medes, not otherwise known; perhaps the Athenians.

  • v8 "when the horn is blown… by the mouth of Michael the archangel" — the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a cry of command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the sound of the trumpet of God. And the dead in Christ will rise first (1 Thessalonians 4:16); the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised (1 Corinthians 15:52).

  • v9 "The mountains and the hills will be brought low" — Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill be made low… and the rough places a plain (Isaiah 40:4).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Bones of the Fathers
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 10

Buried with Their Fathers

1If it were not so, why did the fathers of old, from Adam, Abel and Seth, Noah and Shem, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Joseph, Moses and Aaron, not want to be buried anywhere but in the tomb of their fathers?

2Was it not so that they would rise together at the resurrection with their kin, and that their bones would not be counted with the bones of the evil, the sinners and the heathen?

3You too, do not let your mind go astray when you say, "How will the dead rise after their death, those who are laid in one grave by the [number lost], and whose bones have decayed?"

4When you look into the grave and not a handful of dust is found, and you say, "How will the bones of the dead rise?", you say this in the folly of your heart.

5Do you say that what you sowed will not sprout? What you sowed does sprout.

6So too God, who sowed the souls: they will rise quickly. He does not delay raising them by His life-giving word, for He brought man from where he was not into true being.

7Again He brought him back from being into death, and again from death He brings him back into being.

8God is able to give life and to raise up.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "not want to be buried anywhere but in the tomb of their fathers" — Jacob: let me lie with my fathers. Carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burying place (Genesis 47:30); Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, you shall carry up my bones from here (Genesis 50:25), and Moses took them (Exodus 13:19).

  • v3 "laid in one grave by the [number lost]" — the Ge'ez has babba)), by the followed by two stray marks: a numeral lost in the conversion of the text, like those of 2:6 and 3:26. There is no reading of the Church to restore it from here.

  • v5 "What you sowed does sprout" — the likeness of the seed in 8:22–28.

  • v6 "He brought man from where he was not" — ʾəm-ḫaba ʾi-hallo, the words of 1:11, when he did not exist.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Vine of Sodom
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 11

The Cities Brought Low

1Hermon and its walls have fallen, and those who worship idols in Zebulun and Edom will be brought low then, for God has repaid them according to their evil and the work of their hands. Tyre and Sidon will weep, for the One who will take vengeance on them is near, for their evil and for the idols they made in their youth and did not give up until their old age.

2Because of this God will take vengeance on them, for they practiced lewdness, uncleanness, fornication and idols. The daughters of Judah too will be put to shame, for they did not stand in the commandment of God their Creator.

Jerusalem

3So too, at the resurrection of the dead the shame of Jerusalem will be uncovered, for she did not walk in His law and His judgments, but walked in oppression and the killing of the righteous.

4On that day God will search her with the lamp of His wisdom, and take vengeance on her for all the evil she did in the days of her youth and did not give up in the days of her prime, until her old age.

5She went into the grave and became dust like her fathers of old, who walked in their own will and refused the commandment of God, so that He will take vengeance on them at the resurrection.

6For Moses said of them, "Their vine is from the vine of Sodom,

7and their branches from Gomorrah. Their clusters are clusters of gall, and their grapes are bitter.

8Their wine is the venom of serpents, the deadly venom of asps."

Notes

  • v1 "Hermon and its walls" — ʾArmon wa-ʿarafātihā. ʿAraft is a wall; ʾArmon is taken as Hermon (8:33), though the Hebrew armon is a fortress. The verbs are feminine, said of cities.

  • v3 "oppression and the killing of the righteous" — Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! (Matthew 23:37).

  • v4 "God will search her with the lamp of His wisdom" — At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps (Zephaniah 1:12).

  • vv6–8 "Their vine is from the vine of Sodom" — the song of Moses, word for word: For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah; their grapes are grapes of poison; their clusters are bitter; their wine is the poison of serpents and the cruel venom of asps (Deuteronomy 32:32–33). Chapter 12 builds on it.

chapters.title: Daughter of Jerusalem
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 12

The Vineyard of Sodom

1This is your shame, daughter of Jerusalem, which was written by the prophet: as were the deeds and the sin of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, so are your deeds and your sin, daughter of Jerusalem.

2As with Sodom and Gomorrah, so is your shame: their vineyard was planted in fornication and pride.

3No rain of humility and mercy fell on them, only the rain of pride and fornication, by which their vineyard takes root, with nothing but wrongdoing and robbery and wickedness, the shedding of blood, and the forgetting of the name of God their God.

4They did not know their Creator, only their idols. Their deeds were evil, they took pleasure in the work of their hands, and they practiced lewdness with beasts and with males.

5They did not know God in their deeds, for they blinded their eyes so as not to see and stopped their ears so as not to hear, and so as not to do the will of God or what pleases Him. They are the vineyard of Sodom, the vine of Gomorrah, that bear no sweet cluster.

6Even when they press their grapes, it becomes poison that kills; for from its beginning it was planted in a curse, and its fruit came in a time of trial.

7At no time is there good in the vine of their grapes, for their vineyard was watered with the dew of Sheol, and their branches grew strong in the wind of burning heat.

8Even when it bears fruit and is pressed, it is for ruin and for punishment. It hardens the hearts of those who drink it and makes them cold, far from God,

9and a dwelling for the devil, for they walk in his evil deeds. The vine of Sodom spreads and devours, and climbs onto the mountains and the hills.

10She crowns Baal, whom they worship in the open court, and she sacrifices her sons and her daughters to demons, who do not know evil from good.

11They shed innocent blood, and pour out to carved images from the clusters of the vineyard of Sodom.

12She worships Dagon of the foreigners, and honors him and sacrifices to him from her fat beasts and her flocks, to take pleasure in their drunkenness and their folly, which the demons taught her, so that she would sacrifice to them and do their will,

13and so that she would not know God her Creator, who at all times feeds her and builds her up, from her youth to the days of her prime, and on to the days of her old age and to the day of her death.

God Speaks against Her

14"Again I will take vengeance at the resurrection, and her time will be forever, for she did not turn back to My law or walk in My commandment.

15Let her gods rise, if they are gods indeed, and run with her into Gehenna and save her, when I am angry with her in My wrath and have taken away all her lovers who fornicate with her.

16I made her a shame, for all the reproach and shame she brought on My house and My holy things.

17She bore My name, which was called over her, when they said of her: This is the people of God, the house of the God of Israel, the dwelling of the name of the Most High, Jerusalem, the holy of holies, the city of the great King.

18She boasts in Me as though she were My handmaid and I her Lord; yet she does not fear Me and do My will as a Lord's, but sets herself against Me like a rebel.

19She serves foreign gods, who do not feed her or raise her or clothe her; instead they have become a burden to her, a snare to lead her astray, to take her far from Me.

20She sacrifices to them and eats their sacrifices, pours out drink for them and drinks the wine of their drunkenness, burns incense to them and breathes the fragrance of their incense. They command her, and she obeys them.

21Again, she sacrifices her sons and her daughters, and delights in the work of her hands and the toil of her lips, for she cries out to them for love of them.

22Woe to her on the day of judgment, to her and to the gods she loves and embraces! With them she will go down into Sheol, to the lowest depth, where the worm does not sleep and the fire is not quenched.

23Woe to you, daughter of Jerusalem, put to shame, for you left Me, who created you, and worshiped foreign gods.

24I too will repay you according to your deeds and take vengeance on you according to your contempt, for you provoked Me, scorned to follow Me, and did not make your deeds good.

25I too will disregard you and will not be quick to save you, for you refused My word and did not hold to My counsel, the covenant you made with Me, that you would keep My commandment and I would be with you and save you from all who oppose you, and that you would keep the commandment I gave you, and My ordinance.

26All this you did not keep, and I too have disregarded you, and on the day of judgment I will take vengeance on you. Did I not create you? Yet you did not keep My word and My commandment; and I blessed you, so that you would be Mine.

27But you have made yourself a stranger to Me, as Sodom and Gomorrah made themselves strangers.

28I burned them up in My wrath; and you are from the roots of Sodom and Gomorrah, whom I uprooted, and I blotted out their memory from the earth so that they would not live on in their oppression. For they provoked Me, who created them, by going in to a man's wife, and fornicating lawlessly with males and with beasts as with women.

29There was no fear of God before their eyes, from the least of them to the greatest. No one rebuked his neighbor to make him leave off; they helped one another in every evil deed, and were full of all wrongdoing and robbery, for their deeds were evil.

30Every evil deed was set in their thoughts, pride, robbery and greed.

31Because of this God disregarded them and overthrew their cities. Some He burned with fire down to their foundations, and not one remained of those that perished and were uprooted forever.

32They wait for the day of judgment forever, the great day of judgment, for they were bound by sin; and He will not pity them or have mercy on them, for they provoked Me with their evil deeds.

33I disregarded them; and so you too, daughter of Jerusalem, put to shame, will be bound on the day of judgment, for you will find nothing to excuse yourself with when I seize you in My wrath. For all your deeds are robbery and wickedness, greed and fornication and the speaking of lies, and every way of error and stumbling that I do not delight in.

34I made you for honor, but you made yourself for shame. I called you Mine, but you made yourself another's.

35I chose you for holiness, but you became the devil's; and I will take vengeance on you according to the evil of your deeds.

36I will lengthen an evil vengeance on you, because you did not hear My word or keep My commandment that I gave you on the day I loved you; for I am God, who created you. I will be angry with all sinners like you, and repay them according to their evil on the day of judgment.

37You too I will judge with them, for you did not keep My word and you disregarded My judgment.

38O Sodom and Gomorrah, who have no fear of God in your heart!

39So too, daughter of Jerusalem, you will be judged together, you with her, in the terror of Gehenna, and all who did your deeds; for you will go down together to the Gehenna that is prepared, where there is no way out forever and ever.

40You and she, who did not keep My word and My commandment, will go down together into Sheol on the day of judgment, for you did not keep My word and My commandment.

The Portion of the Righteous

41But as for those who kept My word and My commandment: what the sinners stored up, the righteous will eat, and what the evil acquired, the good will divide as plunder. As God has commanded, the righteous and the good will rejoice and be glad.

42But the sinners and the wrongdoers will weep and mourn for all their offenses, in which they strayed from My commandment.

43Whoever keeps My word and walks in My commandment, he is the one who will eat of the blessing and be honored with Me.

44Everyone who keeps My word and does My commandment will eat the blessing of the earth, and will enter and dwell where the good and upright kings enter."

Notes

  • v1 "as were the deeds and the sin of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, so are your deeds" — Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Give ear to the teaching of our God, you people of Gomorrah! (Isaiah 1:10); Your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done (Ezekiel 16:48).

  • vv5–8 the vineyard — the vine of Sodom from the song of Moses (11:6–8), now Jerusalem's. Isaiah's song of the vineyard: He looked for it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes (Isaiah 5:2).

  • v5 "they blinded their eyes so as not to see and stopped their ears" — Make the heart of this people dull, and their ears heavy, and blind their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears (Isaiah 6:10).

  • v12 "Dagon of the foreigners" — Dāgon za-ʾIloflí. ʾIloflí is the Greek allophyloi, the Philistines (5:20); Dagon is their god (Judges 16:23; 1 Samuel 5:2).

  • v14 "Again I will take vengeance" — from here to the end God speaks of Jerusalem and to her, without a word to say that the speaker has changed.

  • v17 "the city of the great King" — Mount Zion… the city of the great King (Psalm 48:2); Jesus: or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King (Matthew 5:35).

  • v22 "where the worm does not sleep and the fire is not quenched" — their worm shall not die, their fire shall not be quenched (Isaiah 66:24), as Jesus says it of Gehenna (Mark 9:48).

  • v29 "no fear of God before their eyes" — There is no fear of God before his eyes (Psalm 36:1; Romans 3:18).

  • v41 "what the sinners stored up, the righteous will eat" — the sinner's wealth is laid up for the righteous (Proverbs 13:22); he may pile it up, but the righteous will wear it (Job 27:17).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
