and a dwelling for the devil, for they walk in his evil deeds. The vine of Sodom spreads and devours, and climbs onto the mountains and the hills.
She crowns Baal, whom they worship in the open court, and she sacrifices her sons and her daughters to demons, who do not know evil from good.
They shed innocent blood, and pour out to carved images from the clusters of the vineyard of Sodom.

She worships Dagon of the foreigners, and honors him and sacrifices to him from her fat beasts and her flocks, to take pleasure in their drunkenness and their folly, which the demons taught her, so that she would sacrifice to them and do their will,
and so that she would not know God her Creator, who at all times feeds her and builds her up, from her youth to the days of her prime, and on to the days of her old age and to the day of her death.
God Speaks against Her

Let her gods rise, if they are gods indeed, and run with her into Gehenna and save her, when I am angry with her in My wrath and have taken away all her lovers who fornicate with her.
I made her a shame, for all the reproach and shame she brought on My house and My holy things.

She bore My name, which was called over her, when they said of her: This is the people of God, the house of the God of Israel, the dwelling of the name of the Most High, Jerusalem, the holy of holies, the city of the great King.
She boasts in Me as though she were My handmaid and I her Lord; yet she does not fear Me and do My will as a Lord's, but sets herself against Me like a rebel.
She serves foreign gods, who do not feed her or raise her or clothe her; instead they have become a burden to her, a snare to lead her astray, to take her far from Me.

She sacrifices to them and eats their sacrifices, pours out drink for them and drinks the wine of their drunkenness, burns incense to them and breathes the fragrance of their incense. They command her, and she obeys them.
Again, she sacrifices her sons and her daughters, and delights in the work of her hands and the toil of her lips, for she cries out to them for love of them.

Woe to her on the day of judgment, to her and to the gods she loves and embraces! With them she will go down into Sheol, to the lowest depth, where the worm does not sleep and the fire is not quenched.
Woe to you, daughter of Jerusalem, put to shame, for you left Me, who created you, and worshiped foreign gods.
I too will repay you according to your deeds and take vengeance on you according to your contempt, for you provoked Me, scorned to follow Me, and did not make your deeds good.

I too will disregard you and will not be quick to save you, for you refused My word and did not hold to My counsel, the covenant you made with Me, that you would keep My commandment and I would be with you and save you from all who oppose you, and that you would keep the commandment I gave you, and My ordinance.

All this you did not keep, and I too have disregarded you, and on the day of judgment I will take vengeance on you. Did I not create you? Yet you did not keep My word and My commandment; and I blessed you, so that you would be Mine.
But you have made yourself a stranger to Me, as Sodom and Gomorrah made themselves strangers.

I burned them up in My wrath; and you are from the roots of Sodom and Gomorrah, whom I uprooted, and I blotted out their memory from the earth so that they would not live on in their oppression. For they provoked Me, who created them, by going in to a man's wife, and fornicating lawlessly with males and with beasts as with women.

There was no fear of God before their eyes, from the least of them to the greatest. No one rebuked his neighbor to make him leave off; they helped one another in every evil deed, and were full of all wrongdoing and robbery, for their deeds were evil.
Every evil deed was set in their thoughts, pride, robbery and greed.
Because of this God disregarded them and overthrew their cities. Some He burned with fire down to their foundations, and not one remained of those that perished and were uprooted forever.
They wait for the day of judgment forever, the great day of judgment, for they were bound by sin; and He will not pity them or have mercy on them, for they provoked Me with their evil deeds.

I disregarded them; and so you too, daughter of Jerusalem, put to shame, will be bound on the day of judgment, for you will find nothing to excuse yourself with when I seize you in My wrath. For all your deeds are robbery and wickedness, greed and fornication and the speaking of lies, and every way of error and stumbling that I do not delight in.
I made you for honor, but you made yourself for shame. I called you Mine, but you made yourself another's.
I chose you for holiness, but you became the devil's; and I will take vengeance on you according to the evil of your deeds.

I will lengthen an evil vengeance on you, because you did not hear My word or keep My commandment that I gave you on the day I loved you; for I am God, who created you. I will be angry with all sinners like you, and repay them according to their evil on the day of judgment.
You too I will judge with them, for you did not keep My word and you disregarded My judgment.
O Sodom and Gomorrah, who have no fear of God in your heart!

So too, daughter of Jerusalem, you will be judged together, you with her, in the terror of Gehenna, and all who did your deeds; for you will go down together to the Gehenna that is prepared, where there is no way out forever and ever.
You and she, who did not keep My word and My commandment, will go down together into Sheol on the day of judgment, for you did not keep My word and My commandment.
The Portion of the Righteous

But as for those who kept My word and My commandment: what the sinners stored up, the righteous will eat, and what the evil acquired, the good will divide as plunder. As God has commanded, the righteous and the good will rejoice and be glad.
But the sinners and the wrongdoers will weep and mourn for all their offenses, in which they strayed from My commandment.
Whoever keeps My word and walks in My commandment, he is the one who will eat of the blessing and be honored with Me.
Everyone who keeps My word and does My commandment will eat the blessing of the earth, and will enter and dwell where the good and upright kings enter."

chapters.title: The Son of Perdition
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 13

The Proud One to Come

1Tyre and Sidon, and all the borders of the land of Judah that exalt themselves: woe to them now, when I seize them in My wrath, for they will be put to shame and punished.

2God says: For from them will come a proud and arrogant one, a son of perdition, an enemy of righteousness, who stiffens his neck and boasts and does not know his Creator; for I have made him an example of My wrath, to show My power on him, says God, who rules all.

3This is Capernaum and Samaria and Galilee, Syria and Damascus, Cyprus and ʾAkyəyā, and all the region of the Jordan: nations stiff of neck, who walk in their own will, whom darkness and the shadow of death have covered. They do not turn to the fear of God, those whose hearts Sablānyos has covered. Do not obey that proud one!

4Woe to them then, to those who obey the unclean ones and make sacrifices in their name! For they rebel against God who created them, and become like a beast that has no understanding. For that wicked one, the son of perdition, sets up his image in every place, and rejoices in the work of his hands and in the lust of his soul, and in all robbery, wickedness, wrongdoing and deceit, and in all who practice fornication, wickedness and lies.

5In his days it is known that he will do so, for it is numbered by God that he should do this.

6The sun will be darkened and the moon will become blood, the stars will fall from heaven, and every work will perish, by the sign that comes in the last days, so that He may judge the earth and all that is in it according to the work of the hands of those who live in it.

7At the last, the enemy, death, will overthrow him, for he exalted himself against the creation of God and did as he wished for one hour.

8After him there is no authority, "for I will take vengeance," says God, who rules all.

9He too will go down into punishment and the judgment kept for him, on the day he is seized in My wrath; for he drags all who are with him into perdition, punishment and ruin. For I am the One who brings out and brings in to the judgment of Gehenna.

10Let not the mighty boast in his might, for He gives might and strength to the weak, and again gives weakness to the strong and the mighty.

11You will be repaid the vengeance of widows and orphans, for He is the One who holds and avenges those who are oppressed, from the hand of their oppressors.

The Morning Star

12Woe to you who boast and stiffen your neck, and think that He will not seize you or take vengeance on you in My wrath! As it says: "Why has the morning star fallen from heaven, which rises at the time of morning?"

13For he said in his pride and boasting, "I will set my throne above the heavens and the stars, and I will be like the Most High."

14This you dared in your pride, and did not remember God, who created you and made you with His hands. Why did you exalt yourself, only to go down to the lowest depth in the pride of your heart?

15By your pride you became lower than all the angels like you; for they praise their Creator in humility of spirit and do not turn aside from His commandment, for they knew that He made them and created them, and they kept their minds so as not to pass beyond or transgress His commandment.

16But you did evil in the pride of your heart and became lower than your fellows, for you are the keeper of all wrongdoing and robbery, falsehood and wickedness, in which sinners like you walk, the wicked who became of your making. They rebel as you do, and walk in all your will and your command, for you teach them robbery.

17Woe to you and to those you led astray by your temptation: you will go down together into ruin.

18As for you sons of God who went astray after that rebel who leads astray, woe to you! You will go down together into punishment forever, for so you went astray by what he and his demons taught you.

Israel in the Wilderness

19Before this too, while Moses the servant of God was alive, you provoked Him at Horeb, at the waters of testing, at Mount Sinai and at Amalek.

20Again, when you sent spies into the land of inheritance, and they said to you, "Its way is long, and their wall is strong, reaching to heaven; their courts are high, and giants live and dwell there," when they told you this, you wept and despised the word of God, wanting to return to the land of Egypt, to your hard slavery.

21You did not remember God, who saved you from your distress, who did great things in Egypt and led you by the hand of His angel, overshadowing you with a cloud by day so that the sun would not burn you, and giving you light by night with a pillar of fire so that your feet would not stumble in the darkness.

22When Pharaoh and his army frightened you, you cried out and shouted to Moses, and Moses cried out and shouted to God, and by His angel He led you, so that you would not meet Pharaoh's army.

23Them He turned back in torment. For it says, God alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them; and their enemies He covered in the sea at once, and did not leave one survivor of them.

24Israel He brought across on foot through the middle of the sea, and no harm at all came to them from the Egyptians. He brought them to Mount Sinai, and there He fed them manna forty years.

25They grew slack in the worship of God, though He had done so much good for them, for they always provoked God. As it is in the Book of the Generations of the Fathers, it says: "The heart of the sons of men is ashes, and all their works run to wickedness and evil. There is none of them who seeks what is right, only gathering wealth by wrongdoing, swearing falsely, wronging a neighbor, theft and wickedness."

26To this evil they all run all the days of their life. The sons of Israel provoked God greatly, transgressors of the commandments of God from first to last.

Notes

  • vv2, 4 "a son of perdition… sets up his image in every place" — walda ḫagwəl, Paul's name for the one who comes before the day of the Lord: the man of lawlessness… the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself against every so-called god (2 Thessalonians 2:3–4). The image: it was allowed to give breath to the image of the beast (Revelation 13:15).

  • v3 "ʾAkyəyā… Sablānyos" — two names not otherwise known: the first, in a list of lands, may be Achaia; the second covers the hearts of the nations, and is not explained.

  • v6 "The sun will be darkened and the moon will become blood" — The sun shall be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the great and awesome day of the LORD comes (Joel 2:31); the stars will fall from heaven (Matthew 24:29).

  • v7 "the enemy, death" — The last enemy to be destroyed is death (1 Corinthians 15:26). For one hour: the ten kings receive authority as kings for one hour, together with the beast (Revelation 17:12).

  • vv12–13 "Why has the morning star fallen from heaven" — How you are fallen from heaven, O Day Star, son of Dawn!… You said in your heart, "I will ascend to heaven; above the stars of God I will set my throne on high… I will make myself like the Most High" (Isaiah 14:12–14). The Ge'ez has wa-ṣədq, read as wadqa, has fallen.

  • v18 "you sons of God who went astray" — the sons of God saw that the daughters of man were attractive (Genesis 6:2); 1 Enoch tells of the watchers who went astray after their leader (1 Enoch 6–8).

  • v20 "the spies… giants live there" — Numbers 13:28–33, the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large… we saw the Nephilim there. The Ge'ez of this verse is damaged in places (ʿəṣādātihomu nuʿ, ʾəlla yārbəh); their courts are high and giants are the plainest reading.

  • v24 "manna forty years" — the Ge'ez has the digit 4; the number in the verse is the forty years of Exodus 16:35.

  • v25 "The heart of the sons of men is ashes… none of them seeks what is right" — every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually (Genesis 6:5); there is none who does good, not even one (Psalm 14:3). The book cited, maṣḥafa lədata ʾabaw, is not otherwise known.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Noah's Covenant and the Calf
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 14

The Flood and the Covenant

1Even when God punished the first people with the waters of the flood for the sins of the sons of Cain, He drowned the earth with the waters of the flood and washed it of all the filth of the offense of the sons of Cain.

2He destroyed all the wrongdoers, for He said, "I regret that I made man." He destroyed all and left none but four souls; and after that He multiplied them, and they filled the earth and divided the inheritance of their father Adam.

3Noah made a covenant with God, that He would not destroy the earth again with the waters of the flood; and the sons of Noah, that they would not eat what has died or what is torn by beasts, and would not worship foreign gods besides God their Creator; and He, that He would be their God and would not destroy them suddenly for nothing, and would not withhold from them the rain of spring and autumn, and would give food in its season to man and beast, fruits and grass and plants; and they, that they would make their conduct good in all that God loves.

4After He had given them this ordinance, the sons of Israel provoked God with their evil, and did not walk as their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who did not transgress the commandment of God their Creator.

5These sons of Israel were crooked in their deeds, from the least of them to the greatest, and did not keep the commandment of God.

6Even their Levites, their officials and their scribes, all of them, transgress the commandment of God,

7and do not stand in the law and the ordinance of God that Moses commanded them in the book of the law, saying, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,

8and love your neighbor as yourself. Do not worship foreign gods, do not go to another man's wife, do not kill, do not steal,

9do not bear false witness, and do not covet your neighbor's goods, or anything your brother has acquired, whether his donkey or his ox."

10When He commands the sons of Israel this, the harsh ones turn to robbery, falsehood, wrongdoing and wickedness, going to another man's wife, theft, lying and the worship of gods.

The Calf at Horeb

11At Horeb too the sons of Israel provoked God by making a calf that grazes on grass. They bowed down to it and said, "These are our gods, who brought us out of the land of Egypt."

12They rejoiced in the work of their hands; they ate and drank and were filled, and rose up to dance.

13Because of this Moses was angry and came down from Mount Sinai, for God had said to him, "Your people whom you brought out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, have sinned and gone astray. They have made the image of a calf and bowed down to the cast image."

14Moses came down with Joshua his servant, angry with the people. When Joshua heard, he said, "I hear the sound of war in the camp of Israel."

15Moses said to Joshua, "It is not the sound of war, but the sound of men drunk with wine." He came down and broke their image and ground it fine until it was like dust, and threw it into the spring that the sons of Israel drank from at the foot of the mountain.

16Then he commanded the Levites to kill among themselves, for the evil they had done before God.

17They did as he commanded them, knowing that a reproach against God is greater than the killing of themselves, their kin and their fathers.

18Because of this Moses said to them, "Have you so despised God, who fed you and nursed you, and brought you out of the house of slavery, and gave you as an inheritance the land He swore to your fathers, to give to them and to their seed after them?"

19Even there they did not stop provoking God, for they ran into all evil and robbery.

Not like Their Fathers

20They were not like their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who pleased God by the beauty of their conduct from their youth to the days of their prime and their old age, so that He gave them what is on earth and what is in heaven, which He has prepared for those who love Him: here, the land of inheritance that flows with milk and honey; and there, the garden of joy prepared for the righteous, which eye has not seen and ear has not heard and has not entered the heart of man, which God has prepared for those who love Him, for Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, who pleased God in their life.

21But their sons were deniers and evil, who walk in the lust of their heart, and did not hear the word of God, who fed them and nursed them and kept them from their youth.

22They did not remember God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt and saved them from the work of the bricks and the work of bitter slavery.

23They provoked Him greatly, and He raises up against them the foreigners around them, who rise against them and subdue them, as He wills.

Notes

  • v2 "none but four souls" — the Ge'ez has the digit 4. Peter counts eight persons… brought safely through water (1 Peter 3:20): Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives (Genesis 7:13). Four are Noah and his three sons.

  • v3 the covenant with Noah — never again shall there be a flood to destroy the earth (Genesis 9:11); you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood (9:4). The law of what has died or is torn is Leviticus 17:15 and Exodus 22:31. Jubilees tells of Noah giving his sons such commands (Jubilees 7:20–39).

  • vv7–9 "Love the Lord your God… and love your neighbor as yourself" — Deuteronomy 6:5 and Leviticus 19:18, the two that Jesus calls the great commandments (Matthew 22:37–39), joined here to the ten words (Exodus 20:13–17).

  • v11 "a calf that grazes on grass" — They exchanged the glory of God for the image of an ox that eats grass (Psalm 106:20). These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt (Exodus 32:4).

  • v12 "they ate and drank… and rose up to dance" — the people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play (Exodus 32:6), as Paul quotes it (1 Corinthians 10:7).

  • v15 "the sound of men drunk with wine" — ḍəmḍa fāhlu la-wayn. In Exodus Moses says, it is the sound of singing that I hear (Exodus 32:18). The dust thrown into the brook that came down out of the mountain is Deuteronomy 9:21.

  • vv16–17 the Levites — Exodus 32:26–29: Each one of you kill his brother and his companion and his neighbor, and about three thousand fell.

  • v20 "which eye has not seen and ear has not heard" — What no eye has seen, nor ear heard, nor the heart of man imagined, what God has prepared for those who love Him (1 Corinthians 2:9; Isaiah 64:4).

  • v22 "the work of the bricks" — gənfāl: they made their lives bitter with hard service, in mortar and brick (Exodus 1:14).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

They did not remember God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt and saved them from the work of the bricks and the work of bitter slavery.
They provoked Him greatly, and He raises up against them the foreigners around them, who rise against them and subdue them, as He wills.

chapters.title: Mebkyos and His Brothers
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 15

The Threat of Midian

1On that day the people of Midian rose against them and raised their army to make war on Israel. The name of their king was Akrandes, and in the morning he gathered a great army from Syria, Cilicia and Damascus.

2He encamped at the crossing of the Jordan and sent messengers to Israel, saying, "Give me tribute in denarii. If not, I have come to judge you, to plunder your goods, take all your property and carry your children away captive.

3I will carry you off to a country you do not know, and there I will make you hewers of wood and drawers of water.

4Do not boast, saying, 'We are the people of God, and no one can stand against us.' Was it not God who sent me to destroy you and plunder your goods? He sent me to gather all that is yours.

5Did their gods save the other peoples whom I judged, whose goods and property I plundered, whom I killed, and whose offspring and children I carried away captive?

6So I will do to you too, if you do not pay me tribute as I have commanded you." He crossed the Jordan to plunder their goods and their cattle and carry away their wives captive.

7Then the sons of Israel wept bitterly before God, and cried out and wailed, and found no one to help them.

Three Brothers

8Because of this God gave strength to three brothers, whose names were these: Mebkyos, Maccabeus and Judah, who were beautiful in appearance and strong in all their might.

9They heard the sons of Israel weeping and lamenting, and their hearts grieved for all the sons of Israel, the widows and the orphans, their priests and their princes, and all the kindred of Israel, men and women and children, all of them weeping and putting ashes on their heads, and their honored ones putting on sackcloth.

10Those good and handsome brothers agreed to go and save them. They took counsel and said to one another, "Let us go and hand ourselves over to death for these."

11They went boldly, with their swords at their sides and their spears in their hands, ready to fight the giant.

12They arrived while he was at his midday meal. Mebkyos pierced the giant and struck his neck with one blow while the food was in his mouth, and Judah and Maccabeus struck with the sword those on the right and left of their king.

13When their king fell, they all scattered and fled. Their spears went into the hearts of their companions, their bows were broken, and they themselves were crushed.

14The good and handsome brothers were saved, and no harm at all came to them; but the evil ones were crushed among themselves, for God turned punishment back on them.

15They fell and died, and threw away all that was theirs until they crossed the Jordan, and all that was theirs was left behind. When the sons of Israel saw that they had scattered and gone off with their camp, they took the plunder for themselves.

16So God saved the sons of Israel by the hand of Mebkyos and his brothers.

Back to Their Evil

17For a few days the sons of Israel lived pleasing God.

18After that they turned back again to their evil, and the sons of Israel grew slack in worshiping God in purity. He in turn provoked them with a people who do not know Him, who reap the fruit of their fields, ruin their vineyards, take their flocks and slaughter their cattle before their eyes; and they could not save themselves, for they were a people who transgressed the law, who always provoked God at all times.

Notes

  • v1 "Midian… Akrandes" — ʾAkrāndəs, a king known only from this book. Midian oppressed Israel in the days of Gideon (Judges 6:1–6), whose angel the book has named (5:20).

  • v3 "hewers of wood and drawers of water" — what Joshua made the Gibeonites (Joshua 9:21–27).

  • vv4–5 "Was it not God who sent me… Did their gods save the other peoples?" — the words of the Assyrian commander at Jerusalem: Is it without the LORD that I have come up against this place to destroy it? The LORD said to me, Go up against this land (2 Kings 18:25); Has any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria? (18:33).

  • v8 "Mebkyos, Maccabeus and Judah" — Mabkyos, Maqābyos, Yəhudā. These three are not the sons of Maccabeus of chapters 2–4; a Maccabeus is named among them. In 1 Maccabees, Judas called Maccabeus is a son of Mattathias (1 Maccabees 2:4).

  • v11 "the giant" — raʿāytāwi, the word of 5:1 and of the giants of 18:2, said here of Akrandes, the king of v1.

  • v12 "while the food was in his mouth" — the words of Agag's death in 6:32.

  • v13 "Their spears went into the hearts of their companions" — Gideon's night against Midian: the LORD set every man's sword against his comrade and against all the army (Judges 7:22).

  • v18 "a people who do not know Him" — the song of Moses: I will make them jealous with those who are no people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation (Deuteronomy 32:21). The Ge'ez has faʾyaʾammiru, read as ʾəlla ʾi-yaʾammiru, who do not know.

chapters.title: The Nations and the City of God
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 16

The Nations in Their Lands

1The people of Tyre and Sidon, and those who live on the shore of the sea and beyond the river Jordan, and Gilead and Haran, the Canaanites, the Jebusites and the Girgashites, and Edom and the people of Amalek,

2and all the nations in their countries, by their tribes, by their ordinances, by their borders and by the bounds of their lands: all of them are as God has ordained them.

3Among them are some whose conduct is good and who know God.

4Among them are some whose deeds are evil and who do not know God, who created them and made them His own, as they did under Ameneser king of Syria.

5For he will take the strength of Damascus, and divide the plunder of Samaria before the king of Egypt.

6The mountains of Gilead and the valleys of Gilboa, all Samaria and Ṗāṭos of the land of Judah, and those who live in the mountains of Arabia, and Media, Ṗartus, Siwsigyā and Cappadocia,

7and those who live within their borders, peoples stiff of neck, who do not know God and have not kept His commandment:

8He will repay them according to the evil of their deeds and the work of their hands.

Against the City of God

9For the region of Caesarea, the people of Gilead and Amalek join together to fight against the city of God, which is full of righteousness, in which the Holy One of Israel is praised, the God of Israel, the God of hosts, who sits above the chariot of the cherubim, before whom stand ten thousand times ten thousands and thousands of thousands, who serve Him in fear and trembling.

Notes

  • v2 "by their tribes… by the bounds of their lands" — the table of nations: These are the sons of Shem, by their clans, their languages, their lands, and their nations (Genesis 10:31); When the Most High gave to the nations their inheritance… He fixed the borders of the peoples (Deuteronomy 32:8).

  • v4 "Ameneser king of Syria" — ʾAmenesér, a name not otherwise known. Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, took Samaria (2 Kings 17:3–6).

  • v5 "take the strength of Damascus, and divide the plunder of Samaria" — Isaiah: the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria will be carried away before the king of Assyria (Isaiah 8:4). Here it is the king of Egypt.

  • v6 the lands — Ṗāṭos, Ṗartus and Siwsigyā are not otherwise known; Ṗartus may be Parthia, named with Media and Cappadocia in the list of Acts 2:9.

  • v9 "join together to fight against the city of God" — They lay crafty plans against Your people… Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre (Psalm 83:3–7). Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him (Daniel 7:10); who sits above the cherubim (Psalm 80:1), the chariot of the cherubim (1 Chronicles 28:18).

chapters.title: The Teaching of Sablanyos
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 17

Edom and Amalek

1Edom and Amalek joined together. They do not serve God, who holds the judgment of heaven and earth in His hand; they plot to trample His sanctuary, for they are a rebellious people who do not walk in righteousness.

2There is no fear of God before their eyes, only fornication and the shedding of blood, the eating of what is sacrificed, what is torn by beasts and what has died, and everything like this, rejected and defiled.

3They have no faith and no salt, for they are enemies of the good. They do not know God or the way of peace, only robbery and wickedness and every unclean deed, disorder, dancing and play, as their father Sablyānos taught them.

4For he has made them his own with his demons, and he teaches them every evil deed that is his: robbery and wickedness, taking others' goods by wrongdoing, theft, eating what has died and what is torn by beasts, and fornication,

5and everything like this: going to another man's wife, shedding blood, eating what has died and what is sacrificed to idols, killing a human soul by wrongdoing, quarreling, envy and greed, and every evil deed that God does not delight in. This is the teaching that their enemy Sablānyos brings them, to turn them away from the way of God, who holds all the world.

The Way of God

6But the way of God is humility and gentleness, loving one's neighbor, not provoking a brother, love for one another, and peace with all people.

7Do not be people who show favor to persons, robbers, wrongdoers, cheats, men who go to other men's wives, doers of evil and violence against their neighbors, and deceivers who wrong their neighbors,

8who quarrel and stir themselves up, lean toward evil and are quick to lead astray, so as to bring people down into the judgment of punishment forever.

Notes

  • v1 "they plot to trample His sanctuary" — kayda beta maqdasu, the trampling of His holy house. Psalm 83 names Edom… and Amalek among those who say, "Let us take possession for ourselves of the pastures of God" (Psalm 83:6–12).

  • v2 "the eating of what is sacrificed, what is torn by beasts and what has died" — the laws given to Noah's sons (14:3), and the things the apostles forbade the Gentiles: what has been sacrificed to idols, and blood, and what has been strangled (Acts 15:29).

  • v3 "no faith and no salt" — ʾalbomu hāymānot wa-ʾi-məlḥ. Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another (Mark 9:50); Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt (Colossians 4:6).

  • vv3, 5 "Sablyānos… Sablānyos" — the name of 13:3, spelled two ways in this chapter. Here he is their father and their enemy, the teacher of every evil deed, with his demons.

  • v6 "not provoking a brother" — the Ge'ez has wa-ʾamʿəʿo ʾəḫu, and provoking a brother, in a list of the ways of God; it is read as not provoking, the sense the list requires.

chapters.title: The Giants and the Shortened Days
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 18

The Sons of the Giants

1Remember that you are going to God, and all is in His hand, and you will stand with the deeds you have done, to be judged before Him.

2For so too, of old, were the sons of the giants, evil and proud. There was none greater or stronger than they in stature and in the greatness of their arms; yet they did not set God before them, and did not know that He was their Creator, who brought them from where they were not.

3Their fathers, while they were angels, praised God with the angels in the heavens; but when their lust led them astray, they went down into the judgment of punishment forever.

4They took wives from the daughters of the sons of men; for God had made for them the flesh of the sons of men, to expose the folly of their proud hearts and to try them, whether they would keep His commandment and His law.

5They did not keep the commandment, and He brought them down into the judgment of burning fire with the devil their father. Because of them the days of man were shortened, for God was angry with the angels, who sinned like men.

6They drew the sons of men with them, and brought them down into Sheol in their judgment.

The Days of Man

7In the beginning the days of man were [number lost]; they came down to a hundred and twenty years, for the days of man were shortened because the angels went astray with the daughters of Cain.

8God said, "My Spirit will not remain with them, for they are flesh and blood."

9Because of this our days were shortened, and there are some who die while they are children; for our days were shortened from those of our first fathers because of our offense and our sin.

10But for our fathers their days were long, for they kept His commandment and did not provoke God.

11They rebuked their daughters to teach them, and rebuked their sons not to transgress the commandment of God.

12Because of this their days were long in righteousness, for they did not transgress the commandment of God, they and their sons and their daughters.

Notes

  • v2 "the sons of the giants" — daqiqa raʿāyt. The giants of 1 Enoch are the children of the watchers and the daughters of men (1 Enoch 7:2); Numbers knows the sons of Anak, who come from the Nephilim (Numbers 13:33). The same word names the proud giant of 5:1 and 15:11.

  • vv3–5 the angels who took wives — the sons of God saw that the daughters of man were attractive. And they took as their wives any they chose (Genesis 6:2). 1 Enoch tells it at length (1 Enoch 6–10); Jude speaks of the angels who did not stay within their own position of authority… kept in eternal chains under gloomy darkness until the judgment of the great day (Jude 6).

  • v7 "[number lost]… a hundred and twenty years" — numerals lost in the conversion of the text. The first is lost entirely (()). The second is )wa-2: in this text larger numbers are cut short to a digit (forty is 4 in 1:21), so 2 stands for twenty, and ) for the lost hundred. The number is the one of Genesis 6:3.

  • v8 "My Spirit will not remain with them, for they are flesh and blood" — My Spirit shall not abide in man forever, for he is flesh: his days shall be 120 years (Genesis 6:3).

  • v9 "some who die while they are children" — No more shall there be in it an infant who lives but a few days, or an old man who does not fill out his days (Isaiah 65:20).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Daughters of Cain
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 19

Cain and His Daughters

1When the sons of Cain multiplied, they made harps and drums, lyres and pipes, and every kind of play and dancing.

2Daughters were born to Cain, beautiful and lovely, from the wife of Abel the righteous, whom he killed because of her, for she was lovely. After he killed his brother he took her, and his own wife as well.

3He moved away from his father, taking them to the valley of Qefāz, toward Arabia; and the daughters of that lovely woman became lovely like their mother.

4Because of this the angels came down to the children of Cain, and did not wait a single hour, and took for themselves the wives they chose.

5Because of this God was angry with us and with them, for we were drawn with them into error because of their error.

Adam and Eve

6The devil drew our father Adam and our mother Eve into his error, deceiving them, and said to them, "You will be gods, like God your Creator."

7In their folly it seemed true to them, and they transgressed the commandment of their Creator, who brought them from where there was nothing into being, so that they would bow down and praise His holy name.

8Those who made the gift of God their own, their Lord brought them low, and that proud one too.

9As David said, "In the pride of the wicked the poor man is burned"; for by the pride of the devil Adam was condemned with a righteous judgment before God his God.

10So too the angels who went astray after the daughters of Cain drew us into their error, and because of this our days were shortened from the days that God gave our fathers.

Fathers Who Taught Their Children

11But they did good, and no evil came near them, for they held their hearts firm toward God, and taught their sons and their daughters not to turn aside from the commandment of God that they had taught them.

12If they had done it themselves but not told their sons or taught them, it would have profited them nothing.

13As David said, "They did not hide it from their sons, from another generation, but told the praises of God, His might and the wonders He did." As they understood, so they taught their sons, that they too might understand and do it; they entrusted to them the judgment of God, so that they would keep His commandment like their fathers, who pleased God by the beauty of their deeds.

14They did not abandon His commandment, which their fathers entrusted to them in their youth, the fear of God and His judgment, as they had learned it from their fathers.

15Their sons too learned from their fathers to make their conduct good and to give praise to their Creator, for they kept His commandment and loved Him.

16He too hears their prayer and does not disregard them, for He is merciful.

17He turns back His wrath again and again, and does not kindle all His punishment.

Notes

  • v1 "harps and drums, lyres and pipes" — in Genesis it is Jubal, of Cain's line, who was the father of all those who play the lyre and pipe (Genesis 4:21).

  • vv2–3 Cain and Abel's wife — Genesis gives no reason for the murder but the offering (Genesis 4:3–8). The story that the brothers fought over a woman is told in later writings outside the Bible; this book gives it so. Qefāz is a place not otherwise known.

  • v4 "the angels came down to the children of Cain" — 18:3–7. In 1 Enoch the watchers came down… on the summit of Mount Hermon (1 Enoch 6:6).

  • v6 "You will be gods, like God your Creator" — the serpent: you will be like God, knowing good and evil (Genesis 3:5).

  • v9 "In the pride of the wicked the poor man is burned" — Psalm 10:2 in the Greek, ἐν τῷ ὑπερηφανεύεσθαι τὸν ἀσεβῆ ἐμπυρίζεται ὁ πτωχός; the Hebrew has In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor.

  • v13 "They did not hide it from their sons" — We will not hide them from their children, but tell to the coming generation the glorious deeds of the LORD, and His might, and the wonders that He has done… that they should set their hope in God (Psalm 78:4–7).

  • v16 "does not disregard them" — the Ge'ez has la-ʾəllatomu, a word not otherwise known; read with the sense of the verse.

  • v17 "He turns back His wrath again and again" — Yet He, being compassionate, atoned for their iniquity… He restrained His anger often and did not stir up all His wrath (Psalm 78:38).

  • vv1–6 Horovitz — Horovitz's Ge'ez excerpts (1905) have vv1–6 of this chapter and agree with the EOTC text in shape and names (Cain, Qefāz, Adam, Eve).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Remember, Our Brothers
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 20

God Keeps the Righteous

1Remember, our brothers, and do not forget what was told you before: that God keeps the righteousness of those who do good.

2Their fruit will multiply on the earth, and their memory will be for good forever, and their seed will not lack bread on the earth.

3He will save them from the hand of all who oppose them and all their enemies who rise against them; for He contends for them, and does not leave them in the hand of their enemy.

4He is a helper in their distress to those who love His name. He takes them into His keeping, and forgives them all their sins.

Notes

  • v2 "their seed will not lack bread" — I have not seen the righteous forsaken or his children begging for bread (Psalm 37:25); the memory of the righteous is a blessing (Proverbs 10:7).

  • v4 "a helper in their distress to those who love His name" — God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble (Psalm 46:1); Because he holds fast to Me in love, I will deliver him; I will protect him, because he knows My name (Psalm 91:14).

chapters.title: Those Who Trusted in God
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 21

David, Hezekiah and Manasseh

1David trusted in God, and God became his refuge, for he trusted in Him, and He saved him from the hand of Saul the king.

2From Absalom his son, from the foreigners, from the Amalekites and the Edomites, from the Qarneʾon, and from all these who opposed him God saved David, for he trusted in Him and kept His law.

3But the evil kings who did not trust in Him, God did not save, and they were defeated by the hand of their enemy; for victory is from God.

4Hezekiah trusted in God, and He saved him from the hand of the proud Syrian.

5But Manasseh his son was defeated by the hand of his enemy, for he did not put his trust in God. The enemies who defeated Manasseh were not as he was; they bound him and took him to their country, because he did not put his trust in God or fear the One who had honored him, raised him up and made him great.

6At once He withheld from him the gift He had given him, for he did not make his way good before God his God, who would have lengthened his days, stood against his enemy for him, and been to him strength and might, wholeness and a rear guard.

7For trusting in God is better than a great army, and better than trusting in horses, shield and bow.

8Whoever trusts in God will live, and be honored, and be greatly exalted.

9But those who did not trust in God, and trusted in their great wealth, became outcasts from the grace He had given them; for God does not show favor to persons.

10Those who trust in Him He keeps; those who make a fool of Him He makes fools of, and He is not quick to help them in their distress when their enemies oppose them, for they did not make their hearts steadfast in following God and keeping the commandments of God.

11But whoever is steadfast in following God and His commandments and keeping His law, He becomes a refuge to him in his distress.

What God Gives a King Who Loves Him

12He makes him rejoice in the killing of his enemy, in the plunder of his enemies' cattle and in captives from his enemy's country, in the rain of his rainy seasons, the fruit of his fields, the fullness of his granaries and the fruits of his gardens,

13in spring and autumn, in grass and green plants, each in its season, so that your people under your hand may rejoice,

14and eat the labor of others, and be filled with the stores of their enemies, with cattle and oxen and sheep; and eat the labor of others, and take captive the children of their enemies.

15This God does for the one who loves Him; but the one who hates Him He makes a prey for his enemy.

16He binds his hands and his feet and gives him into the hand of his enemy, and makes him a mockery to his enemies, and does not let him rejoice in the seed of his house; for he was a breaker of God's commandment and a shedder of blood.

17He will not stand in the judgment, and God repays the fruit of their deeds to those who do evil, to the doers of evil, when He repays evil.

18As for the doers of good, the king is commanded by God to repay them good by his own hand, and to keep them,

19and to keep the commandment himself, for he is a servant set over all that God created, to do good. God gives them eternal life, and they praise God who created them; and of all He created, none transgresses His commandment but man alone.

Man Alone Transgresses

20All of them know Him and keep to His commandment and His ordinance, as God commanded all of them, who live each in its order.

21But man transgresses against the One who made him king over all the beasts and cattle, and over all the birds that God created,

22whether in the sea or on dry land. All that God created He handed over to our father Adam, to do with as he wished, to eat them like the grass of the earth, to possess them and make them serve him; whether beasts or cattle, God gave them to obey man. As for men who reign, they are to obey God, in the honor He gave them in setting them over all He created, and are to be loyal to Him and obey Him.

23If they transgress His commandment, He strips them of the gift He gave them and gives it to one who does His will, for He is the ruler of heaven and earth.

24He appoints whom He wishes and removes whom He wishes; He kills and makes alive, punishes and has mercy.

25There is no other like Him, and no one is master over Him, for He is Lord of all He created, and there is no other god besides Him in heaven above or on the earth below.

26He appoints and removes, kills and makes alive, punishes and has mercy, makes poor and makes rich.

27He accepts the petition of those who ask Him; and for those who do His will with a pure heart, He hears their prayer and does their will in all they ask Him.

28He commands for them small and great, and all that is theirs in the mountains and hills, the caves and forests, the hollows of the earth, the sea and the dry land.

29All of it belongs to those who do the will of their God. He does not deprive them of His blessing, and He gives them the reward of their praise.

30In heaven too He gives them the honor He prepared for their fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, David, Hezekiah and Samuel, who did not transgress the commandment and the judgment of God,

31so that He may give them the inheritance He swore to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who pleased Him from of old, and that they may rejoice in His kingdom.

Notes

  • v2 "from the foreigners… from the Qarneʾon" — ʾElofəlāwyān, the Philistines (5:20). Qarneʾon is a people not otherwise known.

  • v4 "the proud Syrian" — Soryāwi, the king of Assyria, Sennacherib (2 Kings 19:35–36).

  • vv5–6 Manasseh — the LORD brought upon them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria, who captured Manasseh with hooks and bound him with chains of bronze and brought him to Babylon (2 Chronicles 33:11). Chronicles goes on to his prayer and return; this book does not. Were not as he was, ʾi-konu kamāhu, is literal; the sense of the clause is uncertain.

  • v7 "better than trusting in horses, shield and bow" — Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God (Psalm 20:7); The war horse is a false hope for salvation (Psalm 33:17).

  • v10 "those who make a fool of Him He makes fools of" — yāstaʿabbədəwwo yāstaʿabbədomu, the verb said twice. With the crooked You make Yourself seem tortuous (Psalm 18:26).

  • vv18–19 "the king is commanded by God to repay them good… a servant set over all" — he is God's servant for your good… an avenger who carries out God's wrath on the wrongdoer (Romans 13:4).

  • v20 "who live each in its order" — 1 Enoch: Observe everything that takes place in the sky, how the lights… do not change their paths… But you have not persevered, nor observed the law of the Lord (1 Enoch 2:1; 5:4).

  • v22 "He handed over to our father Adam" — have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing (Genesis 1:28); as I gave you the green plants, I give you everything (Genesis 9:3).

  • v30 "who did not transgress" — the Ge'ez has ʾəlla yətʿaddawu, who transgress, without the negative that the verse requires; read as ʾəlla ʾi-yətʿaddawu.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Remember the Good Kings
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 22

Two Kinds of Names

1Remember, then, the name of those who do good, and do not forget their deeds.

2Be zealous that your name may be like theirs, so that you may rejoice with them in the heavens, in the dwelling of light prepared for the good kings and rulers who did the will of God.

3Again, know and consider the name of the evil kings and rulers, how they are condemned and reviled among men after their death.

4In the heavens too they are judged with the wicked and the rebels who did not do the will of God; for though they saw and heard, they did not mend their way.

Be Good, Gentle and Upright

5As for you, do not walk in the way of the wicked, with whom God was angry for the evil of their deeds; but be good and gentle and upright.

6Judge for righteousness. Do justice to the widow and the orphan, and save them from the hand of the sinners who oppress them.

7Stand by the orphan like a father, to save him from the hand of the one who oppresses him. Be dismayed when the orphan's tears are shed in your presence, so that you will not be dismayed in the sea of fire where the sinners who did not repent are judged.

8Set your feet straight in the way of peace; seek peace and pursue it. For the eyes of God are on His righteous ones, and His ears are open to their prayer.

9But the face of God is against those who do evil, to cut off their memory from the earth, and He leaves none of them on the mountains or within the walls.

10"I will not turn My face away until I destroy those who do not keep My word, for I am a jealous God, who takes vengeance on those who hate Me and on those who did not keep My word.

11I honor those who honor Me and keep My word."

Notes

  • v7 "Stand by the orphan like a father" — Be like a father to orphans, and instead of a husband to their mother; you will then be like a son of the Most High (Sirach 4:10).

  • vv8–9 "seek peace and pursue it. For the eyes of God are on His righteous ones" — Seek peace and pursue it. The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous and His ears toward their cry. The face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to cut off the memory of them from the earth (Psalm 34:14–16).

  • v10 "for I am a jealous God" — for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children… of those who hate Me (Exodus 20:5). From here God speaks.

  • v11 "I honor those who honor Me" — for those who honor Me I will honor (1 Samuel 2:30).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Way of Cain and the Way of Abel
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 23

Cain and Abel

1Do not walk in the way of Cain, who killed his brother. His brother followed him in gentleness, thinking that his brother loved him.

2He killed his brother out of jealousy over a woman; and so do those who practice wrongdoing, jealousy and deceit against their neighbors.

3They walk in the way of Cain, and not in the way of gentle Abel. For Abel was gentle as a lamb, and his blood was like the blood of a pure lamb that is sacrificed to God with a pure heart.

4Those who walk in the way of gentle Abel love God, for they have become gentle like Abel; for God loves everyone who walks in gentleness, like Abel, righteous and gentle.

The Sentence on Their Necks

5But God disregards the evil. Their sentence is kept on their necks, written on their shoulders, and it will be read on the day of judgment before the angels and men and all creation.

6Then the rebels and the wrongdoers who did not do the will of God will be ashamed.

7A word of terror will be given against them, saying, "Cast them into the judgment of burning fire, where there is no way out forever."

Notes

  • vv1–2 Cain — Woe to them! For they walked in the way of Cain (Jude 11). He killed his brother out of jealousy over a woman is the story told in 19:2.

  • v3 "Abel was gentle as a lamb, and his blood…" — By faith Abel offered to God a more acceptable sacrifice than Cain (Hebrews 11:4); the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel (Hebrews 12:24). Jesus calls him righteous Abel (Matthew 23:35).

  • v5 "Their sentence is kept on their necks, written on their shoulders" — dayəmomu… maṣḥuf ba-matākəftihomu. Daniel: the court sat in judgment, and the books were opened (Daniel 7:10).

  • v7 "Cast them into the judgment of burning fire" — Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels (Matthew 25:41).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Men Who Change Their Clothes
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 24

Gideon and the Word of God

1When Gideon trusted in God, with a small army he defeated [number lost], and myriads of soldiers without number, like locusts, and an army of the uncircumcised.

2"Do not trust in foreign gods, for there is no other god besides Me, O kings and rulers.

3For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of your mother's womb, raised you, fed you and clothed you. Why then do you make excuses and worship another god besides Me?

4All this I did for you. What have you given Me? What do I want from you but the salvation of your soul, that you walk in My law, My ordinance and My commandment? Then I will give you the salvation of your soul,"

5says God, who rules all. "Save yourselves from idols, from divination and from sorcerers.

6For the punishment of God comes on those who do this, on those who listen to them, on those who do their will, on those who befriend them, and on those who walk in their command.

A People Who Will Rise against You

7For a people will rise against you who do not know you and will not pity you, and they will eat the fruit of your labor, if you do not do the will of God who made you, as His prophets told, from Samuel the prophet on, and as Ezekiel and Enoch told, and the word of Asaph."

8He said, "Harsh men will come, changing their clothes, with no other law among them but eating and drinking and adorning themselves with gold and silver, and every deed of robbery that God does not delight in.

9They are ready to run to eating and drinking. As soon as they wake from their sleep, from morning to evening they run into evil deeds. For their feet there is no way of peace, only ruin and destruction in their path.

10They do not know the way of peace, and there is no fear of God before their eyes: a crooked and harsh people, who have no salt and no faith, greedy, gluttons, drinkers and drunkards. Their offense is lawless, in lewdness and the shedding of blood, theft, deceit and seizing others' goods by wrongdoing.

11They are accusers without law or justice, with no fear in their faces, for they do not fear God who created them.

12They are not ashamed before the face of a man who sees them, the face of the gray-haired or the face of the old. As soon as they hear of the goods of the world, they make them their own before they see them with their eyes; and once they see them with their eyes, they think they have swallowed them already, for there is no fear of God before their eyes.

13Their rulers too are eaters of bribes. What they said in the morning they do not say again in the evening, for they are liars, and there is no longer truth in their mouth.

14Their kings too run in haste to evil, for they disregard the cries of the poor and the needy, and do not rescue the guests from the hand of those who oppress them.

15Because of this, let kings not be harsh, but let them care for the guest and the oppressed.

16But they are tax-gatherers and rebels who drink blood, and do not spare the kid with its mother or the bird with its chicks; for their way is harsh, and all they see and taste they make their own.

17They do not pity the poor and the old, but love to gather for themselves and seize others' goods by wrongdoing; all they find they gather, to store in their houses and rejoice in.

They Vanish Quickly

18Woe to their souls when God seizes them in His wrath, because they did not make their conduct good in their life! For they vanish quickly, like one who went out from his house and whose trace is not found, and he does not return to his house.

19So they vanish suddenly, all at once, when God disregards them; they perish in their time. For God is not quick to destroy, but is patient, to see whether they will turn to repentance.

20If they do not turn to repentance, God destroys them like those of old before them, who did not keep the commandment of God in purity.

21They are eaters of human flesh and drinkers of blood, with no fear of God at any time, for they gird themselves with violence to run as soon as they rise from their beds, and do not rest from doing wrong,

22from eating and drinking and running into evil and perdition, to destroy the souls of many on the earth."

Notes

  • v1 "Gideon… defeated [number lost]… like locusts… the uncircumcised" — the Ge'ez has )), a numeral lost in the conversion of the text. The Midianites and the Amalekites and all the people of the East lay along the valley like locusts in abundance, and their camels were without number (Judges 7:12); there had fallen 120,000 men who drew the sword (Judges 8:10). Qwəlāfān, the uncircumcised, is the word used of the Philistines.

  • v7 "as His prophets told… Ezekiel and Enoch… and the word of Asaph" — the Ge'ez has wa-nagafa, read as wa-nagara, and the word. Moses: A nation that you have not known shall eat up the fruit of your ground and of all your labors (Deuteronomy 28:33). Enoch is counted among the prophets, as in Jude 14.

  • v8 "changing their clothes" — ʾənza yəwelləṭu ləbsatomu. The verse does not say more.

  • v9 "For their feet there is no way of peace" — Their feet run to evil… desolation and destruction are in their highways. The way of peace they do not know (Isaiah 59:7–8; Romans 3:15–17). Woe to those who rise early in the morning, that they may run after strong drink (Isaiah 5:11).

  • v10 "no salt and no faith" — the words of 17:3.

  • v16 "do not spare the kid with its mother or the bird with its chicks" — the law: If you come across a bird's nest… with young ones or eggs and the mother sitting on them, you shall not take the mother with the young (Deuteronomy 22:6); You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk (Exodus 23:19).

  • v19 "God is not quick to destroy, but is patient" — The Lord is not slow to fulfill His promise as some count slowness, but is patient toward you, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance (2 Peter 3:9).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

They are accusers without law or justice, with no fear in their faces, for they do not fear God who created them.

They are not ashamed before the face of a man who sees them, the face of the gray-haired or the face of the old. As soon as they hear of the goods of the world, they make them their own before they see them with their eyes; and once they see them with their eyes, they think they have swallowed them already, for there is no fear of God before their eyes.
Their rulers too are eaters of bribes. What they said in the morning they do not say again in the evening, for they are liars, and there is no longer truth in their mouth.
Their kings too run in haste to evil, for they disregard the cries of the poor and the needy, and do not rescue the guests from the hand of those who oppress them.
Because of this, let kings not be harsh, but let them care for the guest and the oppressed.
But they are tax-gatherers and rebels who drink blood, and do not spare the kid with its mother or the bird with its chicks; for their way is harsh, and all they see and taste they make their own.
They do not pity the poor and the old, but love to gather for themselves and seize others' goods by wrongdoing; all they find they gather, to store in their houses and rejoice in.
They Vanish Quickly

Woe to their souls when God seizes them in His wrath, because they did not make their conduct good in their life! For they vanish quickly, like one who went out from his house and whose trace is not found, and he does not return to his house.
So they vanish suddenly, all at once, when God disregards them; they perish in their time. For God is not quick to destroy, but is patient, to see whether they will turn to repentance.
If they do not turn to repentance, God destroys them like those of old before them, who did not keep the commandment of God in purity.

They are eaters of human flesh and drinkers of blood, with no fear of God at any time, for they gird themselves with violence to run as soon as they rise from their beds, and do not rest from doing wrong,
from eating and drinking and running into evil and perdition, to destroy the souls of many on the earth."

chapters.title: No One Escapes My Hand
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 25

God Speaks

1"Woe to their souls when I seize them in My wrath," says God, who rules all, "for their way is crooked, and all of them walk in the way of Satan the deceiver.

2They do not know the way of God; they have turned it behind their backs and disregarded My law.

3I too will repay them according to the evil of their deeds. At the last, on the day of judgment, I will take vengeance on them as the evil of their deeds is written before Me, and they will not escape from My hand; for I am God, who kills and makes alive, who punishes and has mercy.

4No one escapes from My hand, beneath the earth or above the heavens, in the sea or the deeps of the waters; for I am God from end to the ends of the world, and the soul of all is in My hand.

5I command the serpent beneath the earth, the great fish in the sea, the birds in the air and the ḥalastəyo in the desert; from end to end, to the ends of the world, it is Mine.

6No one escapes from My hand in heaven above or on the earth below; for I am the One who does wonders and signs before My eyes, and there is none who says to Me, 'Where are You going?' or 'What are You doing?'

7I command above the angels and the archangels; every name that is named is Mine; all the birds of the sky, the beasts of the wild and the cattle are Mine."

The One Who Comes

8The south wind will rise, and the heat of the north, and the Red Sea will roar at the greatness of the majesty of Him who comes to it in the last days.

9For He will judge the living and the dead, with Nubia and Saba, Ethiopia and India, and all their borders and their bounds.

10He shepherds all in gentleness with the rod in His hand. He shepherds His sheep with the rod, for His rod is exalted above all rods.

11His horn is heavier than all horns, His kingdom is exalted above all kingdoms, and His authority holds all the world; He is able to do all, and nothing is too hard for Him.

12He commands the clouds above and makes grass sprout for the cattle below, and gives fruit on the crop.

13He feeds all as He wills, every kind, each with its fruit and its food, all that He created, the qāḥm and the ʾanākwəʿ beneath the earth, the beasts and the cattle above the earth. He grants his prayer to the one who prays, and does not disregard the petition of widows and orphans.

The Wealth of the Wicked and of the Righteous

14Still more He accepts the prayer of the pure, who pray to Him at all times; for the day of the evil is like a stormy wind, and the gathering of the wrongdoers like a cloud that is gone.

15Their joy is like a flying bird, and the beauty of their appearance passes away, with their gold and silver on the earth. Their gold does not profit them; it is only the lamp of the wicked, and the wealth of their clothing is eaten by the moth.

16Their stores of grain and wheat are consumed by moth and weevil, and all passes away like a dream of a day that is gone. As a word that has gone out of the mouth does not return, so is the wealth of sinners; like a passing shadow is the beauty of their living, and like a worn garment is the wealth of sinners before God.

17But the righteous, if they are rich, God does not disregard; for with their wealth they pity the poor, hear the case of the orphan and the needy, clothe the naked from their own clothing, and do not hold back from the produce of their house, which God gave them to give to the guest and the needy.

18They do not pervert the judgment of the faithful, do not withhold the wage of the hired man, and do no wrong in the reckoning of their months or in the measures of their scales; for righteous and honored is the word of God, like one who fills [words lost]

Notes

  • v5 "I command the serpent beneath the earth" — If they hide from My sight at the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them (Amos 9:3). Ḥalastəyo, a creature of the desert, is not otherwise known.

  • v6 "there is none who says to Me, 'What are You doing?'" — none can stay His hand or say to Him, "What have You done?" (Daniel 4:35; Job 9:12).

  • v7 "every name that is named is Mine" — far above all rule and authority and power and dominion, and above every name that is named (Ephesians 1:21); every beast of the forest is Mine, the cattle on a thousand hills (Psalm 50:10).

  • v9 "He will judge the living and the dead, with Nubia and Saba, Ethiopia and India" — Christ Jesus, who is to judge the living and the dead (2 Timothy 4:1); may the kings of Sheba and Seba bring gifts (Psalm 72:10); Cush shall hasten to stretch out her hands to God (Psalm 68:31). Ḥəndake is India, as in 28:38, from India to Ethiopia (Esther 1:1).

  • v10 "He shepherds His sheep with the rod" — Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me (Psalm 23:4); He will rule them with a rod of iron (Revelation 2:27).

  • v13 "the qāḥm and the ʾanākwəʿ beneath the earth" — two kinds of creatures living under the ground, not otherwise known.

  • v15 "it is only the lamp of the wicked… eaten by the moth" — the lamp of the wicked will be put out (Proverbs 13:9); Your riches have rotted and your garments are moth-eaten. Your gold and silver have corroded (James 5:2–3).

  • v18 "do not withhold the wage of the hired man… the measures of their scales" — The wages of a hired worker shall not remain with you all night until the morning… You shall have just balances, just weights (Leviticus 19:13, 36). The Ge'ez breaks off after kama malāʿi za-, like one who fills…

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Fruit of Righteousness
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 26

The Poor and the Dry Tree

1The poor too lie thinking on their beds; and if the rich do not take them in, they become like a dry tree without moisture. Where there is no moisture the root does not sprout, and when there is no root the leaf does not sprout.

2If the leaf does not sprout, it bears no fruit, for the leaf serves the budding of the fruit; and whoever has no fruit has no good deed, for the chief thing in a man is the fruit of righteousness.

3If he does righteousness, he bears uprightness as fruit, and God rejoices in a man who does righteousness and uprightness.

4He grants his prayer to the one who prays, and the labor of his lips, and does not wrong the righteous man for the righteousness he has done,

5nor declare the sinner righteous without repentance, for the evil of the deeds he has done. For God is righteous and loves righteousness, and in judgment He shows no favor to the face of the rich or of the poor; for He is the ruler of heaven and earth, and the soul of all is in His hand.

Notes

  • vv1–2 the tree without moisture — He is like a tree planted by streams of water that yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither (Psalm 1:3). The book turns the likeness to the poor: without the help of the rich, they wither.

  • v2 "the chief thing in a man is the fruit of righteousness" — rəʾsu la-bəʾsi fəre ṣədq, a man's head is the fruit of righteousness. The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life (Proverbs 11:30).

  • v5 "God is righteous and loves righteousness… no favor to the face of the rich or of the poor" — For the LORD is righteous; He loves righteous deeds (Psalm 11:7); You shall not be partial to the poor or defer to the great (Leviticus 19:15).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Creation and the Fall
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 27

The Days of Creation

1He created all the world from nothing. He prepared and set in place the mountains and the hills, made the earth firm on the water, and hedged it with sand so that it would not shake. For the first word of God said, "Let there be light."

2There was light, while the world was darkness. God did His work, prepared and established the world as was fitting and right, and said, "Let there be evening and darkness."

3Again God said, "Let there be light and morning," and there was light. He raised the upper water above the heaven.

4He spread the heaven like a tent cloth and propped it up with the wind, and the lower water He settled beneath the depths of the sea.

5He shut the openings of the sea with sand and made them firm by His Spirit, so that they would not sink into the depths below; and He settled in it creatures and beasts, great creatures in it without number, those that are seen and those that are not seen.

6On the third day God made plants on the dry land, all grass and trees of every kind, and fruits that bear fruit,

7and the tree of life, good to look at and sweet to eat, and grass and every green thing of the earth with its seed in it. He appointed food for all the cattle and the beasts and the birds, and gave nourishment to all He created.

8There was evening and there was morning, and on the fourth day God said, "Let there be light in the firmament of heaven." God made the sun and the moon and the stars and set them in the firmament of heaven, to give light on the earth and to rule it by day and by night.

9From then on the sun and the moon and the stars took their turns by day and by night.

10On the fifth day God created all the creatures and beasts that live in the waters, and all the birds that fly above in the air, and all that is seen and not seen. All this God created.

11On the sixth day He created all the beasts and cattle and creeping things; and when He had created all and set it in order, He created Adam in His image and in His likeness.

12He handed over to him all the beasts and cattle He had created, to reign over them, and also all the cattle and beasts, the fish and the great creatures in the sea,

13the sheep and all the oxen on the earth, and the creatures seen and unseen.

The Garden and the Tree

14He set the son of man, whom He made in His image and in His likeness, in the garden, and commanded him to eat and to work the garden and to praise God there,

15and not to transgress the commandment of God, and not to eat from the tree that makes known good and evil, the tree of death.

16For He said, "On the day you eat from this tree you will surely die."

17By the deceit of the serpent our mother Eve was led astray, and she ate from that tree and gave it to our father Adam.

18He ate from that tree and brought death on himself and on his children.

19God was angry with our father Adam, for he transgressed His commandment and ate from the tree God had commanded him not to eat from. He drove him from the garden and gave him this land of thorns and thistles, which He cursed because of him when he broke His commandment, to work it and eat the reward of his labor by the sweat of his face.

20When God brought him out into this land, Adam turned to grief and sorrow of heart, and began to work the land and to eat by the sweat of his face, in toil and labor.

Notes

  • vv1–13 the days — the order of Genesis 1, with the book's own details: the earth hedged with sand, the heaven spread like a tent cloth (Who stretches out the heavens like a tent, Psalm 104:2), and the sea's bounds: I placed the sand as the boundary for the sea, a perpetual barrier that it cannot pass (Jeremiah 5:22).

  • v3 "the upper water" — the Ge'ez has la-tāḥtāy māy, the lower water, here and in v4. The waters raised above the heaven are the upper waters (the waters that were above the expanse, Genesis 1:7), and v4 places the lower water beneath the sea; v3 is read as the upper.

  • v10 "that live in the waters" — the Ge'ez has wəsta samāyāt, in the heavens, read as wəsta māyāt, in the waters, a difference of one letter: the fifth day is the day of the creatures of the waters and the birds (Genesis 1:20–23).

  • v15 "the tree that makes known good and evil, the tree of death" — of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat (Genesis 2:17).

  • v19 "this land of thorns and thistles… by the sweat of his face" — cursed is the ground because of you… thorns and thistles it shall bring forth for you… By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread (Genesis 3:17–19).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
