chapters.title: From Adam to Esther
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 28

Cain, Seth and Noah

1After that they lived, and Adam's children multiplied. Among them were those who praised God and honored Him and did not transgress His commandment.

2There were prophets too, who prophesied what had been and what would be; and among the children were sinners who lied and did wrong. Cain, Adam's firstborn, was harsh, and killed his brother Abel.

3God was very angry with Cain because he killed his brother Abel; and with the earth too God was angry, because it drank his blood.

4To Cain God said, "Where is Abel your brother?" Cain said in the pride of his heart, "Am I the keeper of Abel my brother?"

5Abel was righteous, and Cain became a sinner by killing his brother Abel the righteous.

6Again Seth the righteous was born; for Adam fathered three daughters and four sons, and among them were the good and the evil.

7Among them were prophets and righteous ones, and among them sinners and the perverse.

8Among them were the good and blessed, who did the will of their father Adam and all that he told Seth his son. So it went from Adam to Noah the righteous, who kept the commandment of God.

9He too entrusted to his sons and told them the will of God, and they told their sons and entrusted to them the will of God, as their father Noah had told them, so that they would not break the commandment of God.

10They lived teaching those who came after them, their sons.

Abraham, Isaac and Jacob

11But Satan fought against those who said yes to him, and spoke to them from within the idols at the tombs of their fathers, the carved images; and they did all that the teacher of evil commanded them.

12They worshiped idols according to their custom, until Abraham the righteous came forth, who did the will of God.

13God made a covenant with him in fire and storm, for he was the first of his kin to walk in the way of righteousness.

14God swore to him to give the land of inheritance to him and to his seed forever.

15So too with Isaac He made a covenant, to give him the inheritance of his father Abraham; and with Jacob too He made a covenant, to give him the inheritance of Isaac his father.

16Their seed after them, the sons of Jacob, He made kings and priests from two tribes of the people of Israel. He blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply greatly."

17He gave them the inheritance of their fathers; yet they did not stop provoking God, while He fed them and loved them in all things.

18When He struck them down, then they sought Him, and turned and rose early to seek God; for God loves them and has mercy on them,

19not for their own sake but for their fathers', for He is merciful and compassionate to all He created.

20He opens His right hand in blessing to satisfy the hungry soul, and opens His eye for mercy, to multiply grain for food.

21He gives food to the young ravens and to all who call on Him; and the sons of Israel too He saves from the hand of their adversaries and enemies when they cry out to Him.

The Saviors He Sent

22Again they turn to provoke Him, and He sends against them the nations, their enemies around them, who destroy them and kill them and take them captive.

23Again they cry out to God with groaning and tears, and He sends them help: at times He saved them by the hand of the prophets,

24and at times by the hand of the judges. When they provoked God, He made them serve their enemies, who plundered them and took them captive.

25David arose and saved them from the hand of the foreigners; and again they provoked God, and He sent against them those who oppressed them.

26At one time He saved them by the hand of Jephthah; and again they forgot God who had saved them, and He sends against them evil enemies who afflict them, take them captive and plunder them, for God repaid them.

27Again they cried out to Him when they were oppressed, and He saved them by the hand of Gideon; and again they provoked God with the work of their hands.

28He too sent again those who afflicted them, and they turned back and wept and cried out to God.

29Again He saved them by the hand of Samson, and they rested a little while; and they rose up to provoke God with the evil they had done before.

30He too sent them others again, who oppressed them; and again they cried out and wept to God to send them help, and He saved them by the hand of Deborah and Barak.

31Again they lived a few days worshiping God; and again they forgot Him and provoked God with their former evil.

32He too sent them others who oppressed them, and again He saved them by the hand of Judith. Again they rested a little, and rose up to provoke God with their evil as before.

33He too raised up nations to rule over them; and they groaned and cried out to God, and He saved them by the hand of Mattathias and his sons, at the corner of the house.

34For he cut off the head of the giant Akemelek, who had come to make war on the land of Judah. When that giant died, his army was scattered and fled, and the sons of Israel killed them as far as the Jabbok, and left none.

In the Land of the Chaldeans

35After that they rested a little, and rose up to provoke God; and He sent them nations to rule them. Again they cried out and groaned to God, and He disregarded their weeping and groaning, for at all times they provoked God and forgot His commandment.

36The nations took them captive and carried them to the land of the Chaldeans, with their priests.

37There too the perverse sons of Israel did not stop provoking God, practicing uncleanness and idols, and they mingled with the nations who had taken them captive.

38There too God was angry at their evil, to destroy them at once. He put wrath into Artaxerxes king of the Chaldeans, so that ten thousand denarii would be brought into the king's treasuries, and so that he would judge them on a day that was fixed, and none of their seed would remain in the land of Persia, from India to Ethiopia.

39So a letter was written by the king's authority, and he gave the seal that was in his hand, so that it would reach every city of Persia,

40and they would kill them on one day, as the king commanded, the day on which he wanted to uproot them; and their plunder, the gold and the silver, he commanded to be brought into the king's treasuries.

41On that day, when the sons of Israel heard it, they cried out and wept and groaned to God, and told Mordecai, and Mordecai told Esther.

42Esther said, "Fast and pray and cry out to God, the God of Israel, the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, wherever you are."

43Mordecai put on sackcloth and put ashes on his head, and fasted; and they prayed and repented wherever the sons of Israel were.

44Esther too mourned greatly. Though she was queen, she put on sackcloth, spread ashes, loosened her hair, and did not anoint herself with perfume as the queens of Persia do; and she wept and cried out to God from the depth of her heart, to the God of her fathers.

45Because of this God gave her favor before Artaxerxes king of Persia, and she made a great feast to the God of her fathers.

46The king and Haman came into the feast Esther had made, and there God repaid Haman as he had wished to do to Mordecai, and they hanged him on a high pole.

47A letter of the king was ordered, that they should leave the Jews alone wherever they were, in all that they wished, and not make them serve, nor rob them, nor wrong them, nor take their goods,

48nor destroy their cities, nor plunder their cattle; and those who loved them honored them, wherever they were in all the land of Persia. For so God has mercy on Israel when they ask and cry out to Him in repentance.

49When they provoke Him, He sends to them nations who oppress them; on that day they weep and groan and cry out for Him to send them help and save them from the hand of those who afflict them.

Notes

  • v6 "three daughters and four sons" — the Ge'ez has the digits 3 and 4. In this text larger numbers are often cut to a digit (1:21), so these may be shortened; they are rendered as they stand. Genesis says only that Adam fathered other sons and daughters (Genesis 5:4).

  • v13 "a covenant with him in fire and storm" — a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch passed between these pieces. On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram (Genesis 15:17–18).

  • vv18–21 — When He killed them, they sought Him; they repented and sought God earnestly (Psalm 78:34); You open Your hand; You satisfy the desire of every living thing (Psalm 145:16); He gives to the beasts their food, and to the young ravens that cry (Psalm 147:9).

  • vv22–32 the saviors — the round of Judges, the LORD raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand of those who plundered them (Judges 2:16), told in the book's own order: David before Jephthah, Gideon, Samson, Deborah and Barak, and then Judith.

  • vv33–34 "Mattathias and his sons… the giant Akemelek" — Mattathias is the father of Judas Maccabeus (1 Maccabees 2:1–5). Akemelek, the giant (raʿāytāwi, 5:1), is not named elsewhere. The Ge'ez verb at the head of v34, heṗa, is not otherwise known; cut off is the plain sense with the head of the giant. The verse ends without its stop: wa-ʾi-yātrafu, and they left none.

  • vv38–46 Esther — the story of Esther as the Greek tells it: the king is Artaxerxes (Greek Esther 1:1), and Esther took off her splendid apparel… and instead of costly perfumes covered her head with ashes (Greek Esther 14:2, English numbering). Here he is called king of the Chaldeans (v38) and king of Persia (v45). Ten thousand denarii: in Esther Haman offers ten thousand talents of silver (Esther 3:9).

  • v46 "a high pole" — diba ʿəḍ nawwāḫ, the pole fifty cubits high of Esther 5:14 and 7:9–10.

speech.text: 1 Meqabyan 28
Cain, Seth and Noah
After that they lived, and Adam's children multiplied. Among them were those who praised God and honored Him and did not transgress His commandment.
There were prophets too, who prophesied what had been and what would be; and among the children were sinners who lied and did wrong. Cain, Adam's firstborn, was harsh, and killed his brother Abel.
God was very angry with Cain because he killed his brother Abel; and with the earth too God was angry, because it drank his blood.
To Cain God said, "Where is Abel your brother?" Cain said in the pride of his heart, "Am I the keeper of Abel my brother?"
Abel was righteous, and Cain became a sinner by killing his brother Abel the righteous.
Again Seth the righteous was born; for Adam fathered three daughters and four sons, and among them were the good and the evil.
Among them were prophets and righteous ones, and among them sinners and the perverse.
Among them were the good and blessed, who did the will of their father Adam and all that he told Seth his son. So it went from Adam to Noah the righteous, who kept the commandment of God.

He too entrusted to his sons and told them the will of God, and they told their sons and entrusted to them the will of God, as their father Noah had told them, so that they would not break the commandment of God.
They lived teaching those who came after them, their sons.
Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
But Satan fought against those who said yes to him, and spoke to them from within the idols at the tombs of their fathers, the carved images; and they did all that the teacher of evil commanded them.
They worshiped idols according to their custom, until Abraham the righteous came forth, who did the will of God.
God made a covenant with him in fire and storm, for he was the first of his kin to walk in the way of righteousness.
God swore to him to give the land of inheritance to him and to his seed forever.
So too with Isaac He made a covenant, to give him the inheritance of his father Abraham; and with Jacob too He made a covenant, to give him the inheritance of Isaac his father.
Their seed after them, the sons of Jacob, He made kings and priests from two tribes of the people of Israel. He blessed them and said to them, "Be fruitful and multiply greatly."
He gave them the inheritance of their fathers; yet they did not stop provoking God, while He fed them and loved them in all things.
When He struck them down, then they sought Him, and turned and rose early to seek God; for God loves them and has mercy on them,
not for their own sake but for their fathers', for He is merciful and compassionate to all He created.
He opens His right hand in blessing to satisfy the hungry soul, and opens His eye for mercy, to multiply grain for food.
He gives food to the young ravens and to all who call on Him; and the sons of Israel too He saves from the hand of their adversaries and enemies when they cry out to Him.
The Saviors He Sent
Again they turn to provoke Him, and He sends against them the nations, their enemies around them, who destroy them and kill them and take them captive.
Again they cry out to God with groaning and tears, and He sends them help: at times He saved them by the hand of the prophets,
and at times by the hand of the judges. When they provoked God, He made them serve their enemies, who plundered them and took them captive.
David arose and saved them from the hand of the foreigners; and again they provoked God, and He sent against them those who oppressed them.

At one time He saved them by the hand of Jephthah; and again they forgot God who had saved them, and He sends against them evil enemies who afflict them, take them captive and plunder them, for God repaid them.
Again they cried out to Him when they were oppressed, and He saved them by the hand of Gideon; and again they provoked God with the work of their hands.
He too sent again those who afflicted them, and they turned back and wept and cried out to God.
Again He saved them by the hand of Samson, and they rested a little while; and they rose up to provoke God with the evil they had done before.
He too sent them others again, who oppressed them; and again they cried out and wept to God to send them help, and He saved them by the hand of Deborah and Barak.
Again they lived a few days worshiping God; and again they forgot Him and provoked God with their former evil.
He too sent them others who oppressed them, and again He saved them by the hand of Judith. Again they rested a little, and rose up to provoke God with their evil as before.
He too raised up nations to rule over them; and they groaned and cried out to God, and He saved them by the hand of Mattathias and his sons, at the corner of the house.

For he cut off the head of the giant Akemelek, who had come to make war on the land of Judah. When that giant died, his army was scattered and fled, and the sons of Israel killed them as far as the Jabbok, and left none.
In the Land of the Chaldeans

After that they rested a little, and rose up to provoke God; and He sent them nations to rule them. Again they cried out and groaned to God, and He disregarded their weeping and groaning, for at all times they provoked God and forgot His commandment.
The nations took them captive and carried them to the land of the Chaldeans, with their priests.
There too the perverse sons of Israel did not stop provoking God, practicing uncleanness and idols, and they mingled with the nations who had taken them captive.

There too God was angry at their evil, to destroy them at once. He put wrath into Artaxerxes king of the Chaldeans, so that ten thousand denarii would be brought into the king's treasuries, and so that he would judge them on a day that was fixed, and none of their seed would remain in the land of Persia, from India to Ethiopia.
So a letter was written by the king's authority, and he gave the seal that was in his hand, so that it would reach every city of Persia,

and they would kill them on one day, as the king commanded, the day on which he wanted to uproot them; and their plunder, the gold and the silver, he commanded to be brought into the king's treasuries.
On that day, when the sons of Israel heard it, they cried out and wept and groaned to God, and told Mordecai, and Mordecai told Esther.
Esther said, "Fast and pray and cry out to God, the God of Israel, the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, wherever you are."
Mordecai put on sackcloth and put ashes on his head, and fasted; and they prayed and repented wherever the sons of Israel were.

Esther too mourned greatly. Though she was queen, she put on sackcloth, spread ashes, loosened her hair, and did not anoint herself with perfume as the queens of Persia do; and she wept and cried out to God from the depth of her heart, to the God of her fathers.
Because of this God gave her favor before Artaxerxes king of Persia, and she made a great feast to the God of her fathers.
The king and Haman came into the feast Esther had made, and there God repaid Haman as he had wished to do to Mordecai, and they hanged him on a high pole.
A letter of the king was ordered, that they should leave the Jews alone wherever they were, in all that they wished, and not make them serve, nor rob them, nor wrong them, nor take their goods,

nor destroy their cities, nor plunder their cattle; and those who loved them honored them, wherever they were in all the land of Persia. For so God has mercy on Israel when they ask and cry out to Him in repentance.
When they provoke Him, He sends to them nations who oppress them; on that day they weep and groan and cry out for Him to send them help and save them from the hand of those who afflict them.

chapters.title: Do Good to Me
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 29

Out of Egypt

1Even when Egypt oppressed the sons of Israel with mortar and the making of bricks, with every kind of work they forced on them, and with bricks without straw,

2and set taskmasters over them and made them work, they cried out to God to save them from all their brickmaking for Egypt.

3On that day He sent them help, Moses and Aaron, and they saved them from the work of the bricks; for God sent them to bring His people out of the house of slavery of Pharaoh king of Egypt, who in his pride refused to let the people go, so that they would not serve God and sacrifice to Him in the wilderness.

4For God disregards the proud, and because of Pharaoh's pride God drowned him with his army in the Red Sea.

5So too with those who disregard the word of God while they are kings and rulers, and do not do well in all that He appointed them and made them king for: to do His will, to give their wage to those who serve well, and to honor His great name.

God Speaks to Kings

6"If they set My kingdom right, I too will set their kingdom right," says God, who rules all.

7"Do good to Me, and I will do good to you. Keep My commandment, and I will keep your soul. Walk in My commandment, and I will walk as your heart desires.

8Love Me, and I will love your life. Take refuge in Me, and I will be your strength.

9Trust in Me, and I will save you," says God, who rules all.

10"Do not walk crookedly. Draw near to Me, and I will draw you near, for I love straight paths," says God, who rules all. "Cleanse your hands, you sinners and you perverse, and put away the evil of your heart.

11I too will put away My wrath from you and turn to you with compassion and mercy.

12I will remove far from you the enemy, the rebels who do wrong, as I saved David My servant from the many trials his enemy brought on him, from the hand of Goliath the giant, from the hand of Saul, who sought to kill him, and from the hand of Absalom his son, who wanted to take his kingdom.

13So too I saved those who do My will, keep My commandment and are patient in My law. I gave them honor as an inheritance and made them reign above all, so that they may rejoice in this world and in the world to come."

Samuel

14They will be partners with the blessed kings who pleased God by the beauty of their life, like Samuel, whom God chose while he was still a child, from his youth, for the beauty of his life.

15God spoke to him so that he would tell Eli, the old priest; and good were the deeds of Samuel the prophet while he served in the house of the Lord God.

16When he grew up in the house of God, serving there, God made him one to rule the people and to anoint kings at the command of God. He put the anointing oil of the kingdom into his hand, since he did the will of God his God, for he pleased Him, to make kings over the people God had chosen from the sons of Israel.

17While Saul was still reigning, God said to Samuel the prophet, "Go, anoint David son of Jesse, of the house of Judah, for I am pleased with him."

Notes

  • v1 "bricks without straw" — ṭəbyāt za-ʾənbala ḫaśar: You shall no longer give the people straw to make bricks… let them go and gather straw for themselves (Exodus 5:7).

  • vv7–9 "Do good to Me, and I will do good to you" — the book's own pattern of command and promise. Those who honor Me I will honor (1 Samuel 2:30).

  • v10 "Draw near to Me, and I will draw you near… Cleanse your hands, you sinners" — Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded (James 4:8); Return to Me, says the LORD of hosts, and I will return to you (Zechariah 1:3).

  • v12 "Goliath the giant" — Golyād raʿāytāwi: the word of 5:1, 15:11 and 18:2, said of the giant David killed (1 Samuel 17).

  • v15 "so that he would tell Eli" — the word of the LORD that came to the boy Samuel in the night, against Eli's house (1 Samuel 3:1–18).

  • v17 "Go, anoint David son of Jesse… for I am pleased with him" — Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided for Myself a king among his sons (1 Samuel 16:1).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The House of Saul
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 30

God Speaks of Saul

1"I hated the house of Saul, for he provoked Me by transgressing My word.

2I too disregarded him, and I will not again make a king from his house, for he did not keep My word.

3So too with those who do not keep My word and do not walk in My law and My ordinance: I will withhold from them My gift, and My kingdom from their seed, forever.

4I regret it, so as not to make them great again, but only to destroy them; for when I made them great, they did not make Me great, and when I honored them, they did not honor Me.

5When I did good to them, they did not do good to Me; when I taught them, they would not learn from Me.

6For I made them head over all, but they did not make Me head over them; and when I honored them above all, they did not honor Me or keep My commandment.

7So I took back the gift I had given them, and I will not give it back to them, as I swore in My wrath. Whoever honors Me I will honor, and whoever loves Me I will love." So says God, who rules all.

8"But those who do not honor Me and have not kept My commandment I will strip of the gift I gave them."

All Is Mine

9God, who rules all, says: "Whoever loves Me I love, and whoever makes Me great I make great.

10For I am God, who judges all, and no one escapes from My hand in heaven above or on the earth below; for I am God, who kills and makes alive, who punishes and has mercy.

11Greatness and honor are Mine. Whom I love I honor, and whom I hate I bring low.

12I am the One who has mercy on those who love Me and remember My name at all times. For poor and rich alike, I am the steward of food,

13and not for man alone, but for the cattle and the birds, the beasts, the fish in the sea and the serpents,

14the great creatures of the sea, the ḥargaṣāt, the ʾəngwatāt, Behemoth and the qwarnanʿāt,

15and all that moves in the water and all that flies above the wind: it is Mine.

16I am the One who feeds all who seek Me with what is fitting and what they desire."

Notes

  • v4 "I regret it" — ʾənessəḥ: I regret that I have made Saul king, for he has turned back from following Me (1 Samuel 15:11).

  • v5 "when I taught them, they would not learn from Me" — maharkəwwomu, I taught them. Written with the other h, the verb is have mercy; the verse is read with the spelling as it stands.

  • v7 "Whoever honors Me I will honor" — for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed (1 Samuel 2:30), the word against the house of Eli.

  • vv13–15 "the steward of food… for the cattle and the birds… Behemoth" — These all look to You, to give them their food in due season (Psalm 104:27); Behold, Behemoth, which I made as I made you (Job 40:15). Ḥargaṣāt, ʾəngwatāt and qwarnanʿāt are creatures of the waters not otherwise known.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Not without My Will
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 31

God Speaks

1"Kings are not appointed without My will, the poor are not made poor without My command, and the mighty are not made strong without My will.

2I gave David favor, and wisdom to Solomon, and I added years to Hezekiah.

3I shortened the days of Goliath; I gave strength to Samson, and again I weakened his strength.

4I saved David My servant from the hand of Goliath the giant,

5and also from the hand of Saul the king, and also from the hand of another giant who opposed him, and from the hand of all who opposed and resisted him, for he kept My commandment.

6I loved him; and all who keep My commandment, kings and rulers, I too love them and give them strength and victory over their enemies, for they too have made Me glad.

7Again I give them the land of inheritance that I swore to their fathers, a pure and bright land, so that they may inherit the land of their fathers."

Notes

  • v2 "wisdom to Solomon… years to Hezekiah" — I give you a wise and discerning mind (1 Kings 3:12); I will add fifteen years to your life (2 Kings 20:6).

  • v3 "I gave strength to Samson, and again I weakened his strength" — If my head is shaved, then my strength will leave me (Judges 16:17); the LORD had left him (16:20).

  • v5 "another giant who opposed him" — Ishbi-benob, one of the descendants of the giants… thought to kill David. But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid (2 Samuel 21:16–17).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Hear My Word, Kings
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 32

What God Gave Israel

1"You too, kings and rulers, hear My word and keep My commandment," says God, who rules all. "For the sons of Israel provoked Me and worshiped other gods, though I was the Lord their God, who kept them and saved them and raised them up from the time of their fathers, and fed them with all they desired.

2I made them ride on the heights of the earth and fed them with the blessing of the earth: as was fitting, vineyards they had not planted, olive oil, and cisterns of sweet water they had not dug,

3drops of honey and the milk of sheep with the finest of the wheat, fine garments and everything they desired.

4Nothing they asked of Me did I withhold from them."

Notes

  • vv2–3 "vineyards they had not planted… cisterns… they had not dug" — cisterns that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant (Deuteronomy 6:11).

  • vv2–3 "the heights of the earth… honey… the finest of the wheat" — the song of Moses: He made him ride on the high places of the land… He made him suck honey out of the rock… curds from the herd, and milk from the flock… with the very finest of the wheat (Deuteronomy 32:13–14), as in 5:22–23.

  • v4 "Nothing they asked of Me did I withhold" — He gave them what they asked, but sent a wasting disease among them (Psalm 106:15).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: You Are a Man
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 33

Manna and Disregard

1"Again, I fed them manna in the wilderness, bread, as David said, 'Man ate the bread of His angels.' All this I did for them, so that they would serve Me in righteousness and uprightness.

2But they did not serve Me, and I too disregarded them," says God, who rules all. "They provoked Me and walked in ways that were not Mine.

3I too repay them according to their deeds, and according to the work of their hands I disregarded them; for they grew slack in serving Me and did not hold to My ordinance and My counsel. I brought them down into the judgment of punishment from heaven.

4On earth too I shorten their days, for they did not keep My commandment, and I am angry with them.

To the King

5You too, king, are you not a man, who dies and decays, who tomorrow will be worms and maggots and ashes?

6Yet now you boast and exalt yourself as though you would never die.

7You are a man, seen alive today and dead tomorrow," says God, who rules all.

8"If you keep My word and My commandment, I will give you the holy city as an inheritance, with the honored kings who did My will, whose dwelling is bright and whose crowns are beautiful, whose thrones of gold and silver are prepared for those who sit on them.

9You will rejoice in His city, the dwelling that is near for the doers of good.

10But the doers of evil are not worthy to enter that city where the honored kings enter,

11for they did not keep My word and My ordinance," says God, who rules all.

Notes

  • v1 "Man ate the bread of His angels" — Man ate of the bread of the angels (Psalm 78:25), as the Greek reads it; the Hebrew has the bread of the mighty.

  • v5 "who tomorrow will be worms and maggots and ashes" — the word to the king of Babylon: maggots are laid as a bed beneath you, and worms are your covers (Isaiah 14:11); a man, who is a maggot, and the son of man, who is a worm (Job 25:6).

  • vv6–7 "as though you would never die… seen alive today and dead tomorrow" — the king of today will die tomorrow (Sirach 10:10); you do not know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist (James 4:14), as in 4:18.

  • v8 "the holy city… thrones of gold" — the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God (Revelation 21:2); the dwelling of the good kings in 6:2–10.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: The Day of God
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 34

Kingdom against Kingdom

1The kingdom of the Medes will perish, and the kingdom of Rome will grow very strong over the kingdom of Macedonia, the kingdom of Nineveh and the kingdom of Persia;

2and the kingdom of Ethiopia over the kingdom of Alexandria, and the kingdom of Moab over Amalek; for they will rise.

3Brother will rise against brother, and God will take vengeance as He has spoken against them, so that they destroy one another.

4He said, "Kingdom will rise against kingdom, people against people and country against country."

5There will be tumult and killing, famine and plague and earthquake, and the rains will fail; for peace and love have been taken away, and the punishment of God has come down on the earth.

6The day of God draws near suddenly, like lightning that appears from the east to the west.

7Then each will be repaid according to his deeds, the labor of his hands and the fruit of his deeds; for God Himself has said, "On the day of judgment I will take vengeance on them, in the time when their foot slips, for the day of their reckoning is near."

8On that day God will bring the doers of evil who did not walk in His law to an end, into eternal judgment: the people of Judah, Cyprus, Samaria, Damascus and the people of Babylon,

9those who live in the islands of Arabia, India, Nubia, Saba, Egypt and Ethiopia, and all who live in them.

Then They Will Know Me

10"Then they will know Me, that I am God, who judges heaven and earth. I am the One who gives honor and favor; I am the One who kills and makes alive.

11I am the One who makes the sun rise and sends it to its setting; I am the One who brings good and evil.

12I am the One who brings a people you do not know, who will eat the fruit of your labor and the herds of your cattle and your sheep.

13They will dash your children before you and take them captive, and you will not be able to save them; and they will eat what you have sweated for and your green things, for you did not fear the commandment of God that you heard, and the Spirit of God was not mingled in you."

14Whoever has the Spirit of God dwelling in him knows all things, as Nebuchadnezzar said to Daniel the prophet, "I see that the Spirit of God is in you."

15For whoever has the Spirit of God knows all; even what is hidden is uncovered to him, and nothing is hidden from the Spirit of God, but He knows all, the hidden and the open.

16We are men, who will die tomorrow, and our deeds will be uncovered, all that we did in secret.

17As gold and silver are tested in fire, so sinners will be tested on the last day, for they did not keep the commandment of God.

18Then the deeds of all the sons of Israel and of all the nations will be tested.

Notes

  • vv1–2 the kingdoms — Daniel's four kingdoms, each rising over the last (Daniel 2:36–45; 7:17–27), here with Rome over Macedonia, Nineveh and Persia, and Ethiopia over Alexandria.

  • vv4–6 "Kingdom will rise against kingdom… like lightning that appears from the east to the west" — Jesus: nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places (Matthew 24:7); as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man (24:27).

  • v7 — the word of the song of Moses (Deuteronomy 32:35), quoted in 7:28 as well.

  • v11 "I am the One who brings good and evil" — I form light and create darkness; I make well-being and create calamity; I am the LORD, who does all these things (Isaiah 45:7).

  • vv12–13 "a people you do not know, who will eat the fruit of your labor" — A nation that you have not known shall eat up the fruit of your ground… Your sons and your daughters shall be given to another people (Deuteronomy 28:32–33).

  • v14 "I see that the Spirit of God is in you" — Nebuchadnezzar to Daniel: in whom is the spirit of the holy gods (Daniel 4:8–9).

  • v15 "nothing is hidden from the Spirit of God" — the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God (1 Corinthians 2:10); nothing is covered up that will not be revealed (Luke 12:2).

  • v17 "As gold and silver are tested in fire" — the fire will test what sort of work each one has done (1 Corinthians 3:13); gold that perishes though it is tested by fire (1 Peter 1:7).

chapters.title: Woe to the Mighty of Israel
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 35

Woe to You

1Woe to you, mighty ones of Israel, for God is angry with you, because you did not do justice for the orphan.

2Woe to you who go to the house of the wine-seller morning and evening, and get drunk and turn justice aside, and do not hear the case of the orphan and the widows, and live in lewdness and robbery!

3So God says to the mighty of Israel: "Woe to you if you do not walk in My commandment and keep My word, and love what I love.

4I will bring on you punishment and trial and sickness, and you will waste away like what the moth and the worm eat, and no trace of you will be found within your borders.

5Your country will become a desert, and everyone who saw it before will clap his hands and hiss over it, saying, 'Is this not the city that was full of blessing and every good thing? Is this what God has done to it, for the evil of those who live in it?'"

The Proud City

6Woe to her, for she lifted up her heart and raised her head and stretched out her neck, until God brought her low to the dust of the earth for the pride of those who live in her. She became a desert, and thorns and thistles sprouted on her.

7She became a ruin and a heap, a forest and a desert, and the beasts live in her.

8She became a terror to those who pass through her, for the wrath of God fell on her, and she drank from the cup of His wrath, because of the pride of her heart and the evil of those who live in her.

Notes

  • v2 "who go to the house of the wine-seller morning and evening" — Woe to those who rise early in the morning, that they may run after strong drink, who tarry late into the evening as wine inflames them!… who acquit the guilty for a bribe, and deprive the innocent of his right (Isaiah 5:11, 23).

  • v4 "like what the moth and the worm eat" — I am like a moth to Ephraim, and like dry rot to the house of Judah (Hosea 5:12).

  • v5 "clap his hands and hiss over it… Is this the city" — All who pass along the way clap their hands at you; they hiss and wag their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty?" (Lamentations 2:15); Why has the LORD done thus to this land? (Deuteronomy 29:24).

  • vv7–8 "the beasts live in her… she drank from the cup of His wrath" — wild animals will lie down there (Isaiah 13:21); you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of His wrath (Isaiah 51:17).

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.

chapters.title: Like the Sand and Like the Stars
chapters.html:
1 Meqabyan 36

Do Not Boast

1Do not boast, you Macedonians, and do not stiffen your neck, you Amalekites, for there is God, who takes vengeance on you.

2For you will be raised up to heaven, and you will go down to Sheol.

3When Israel first went into the land of Egypt, in the kingdom of the Medes and the Moabites, He said, "Do not boast; it is not fitting for you to bring reproach on God by reproaching Him."

4You too, son of a slave woman, Ishmaelite, why do you stretch out your neck toward what is not yours? Do you not remember that God will judge you on the day of judgment, when He rises to judge the earth?

5Then you will be repaid according to the work of your hands. "Why do you lift up your heart and stretch out your neck?" says God, who rules all.

6"I too will reproach you as you reproached those who were not yours, wherever I sent you; for you do whatever you please, and you do evil.

7So I too will do to you," says God, who rules all. "But if you do good and love what I love, I too will hear you in all you ask of Me,

8and I will do your will if you do My will. Your enemy will not stand against you, and I will bless your work, your seed and your children.

9I will bless the herds of your cattle and your sheep, and bless all you put your hand to, if you walk in My commandment and do what I love," says God, who rules all.

10"But if you do not do My will and do not walk in My commandment, My judgment will find you, all this judgment of Mine that was spoken before, and you will not be able to escape My wrath that comes on you at all times, for you did not submit to My commandment or walk in My judgment.

11You did not prefer what I prefer, and you turned aside from praising Me and serving Me, though I created you from where you were not.

12I gave you honor and praise among the people under you, so that you could do all you wished: to kill and to keep alive, to build and to pull down, to honor and to bring low, to raise up and to put down. It is yours."

The Way of Salvation

13If you do the will of God and walk in His commandments, He will love you, so that you will rejoice with Him in His kingdom and have a share with those who have inherited the holy city.

14For He said, "If they are patient with Me, I will give them honor and favor as an inheritance and make them rejoice in My house of prayer, and they will be chosen and pleasing like a sacrifice of offering," says God, who rules all.

15Do not grow slack in doing good and in the way of salvation, so that you may cross over from death to life.

16Those who keep to doing good God takes into His keeping in every good thing, so that they may be His servants, like Job, whom God kept from all evil,

17and like Abraham, whom He saved when he struck down the kings, as He saved Moses from the hand of Pharaoh; and He saved Abraham from the hand of the Canaanites, among whom he lived, while they troubled his soul evening and morning, day and night, to bring him down to their idols.

18He was patient, refusing them in what was theirs, the carved images, while they dragged at him.

19He kept refusing them, and feared God who created him; for Abraham was faithful to God, in whom he believed from his youth.

20He did not lessen his worship of God until the year of his death, for he loved God greatly and did not transgress His commandment until the day of his death; and he taught his sons to keep the commandment of God.

21They too did not transgress His commandment, as their father had done. The seed of Abraham, His servants, Isaac and Jacob, did not transgress the commandment of God; of them God spoke, saying to His angels, "I have friends

22on the earth: Abraham My beloved, Isaac My servant, and Jacob in whom My soul delights, in whom I am glorified," says God, who rules all.

Israel in the Wilderness

23The sons of Israel provoked Him greatly, again and again, while He was patient with them and fed them manna in the wilderness.

24Their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell, for they fed on manna, which is the bread of knowledge.

25But their heart was always far from God, and they had no hope of salvation, for from of old they were doers of evil.

26They were not like their fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who pleased God by the beauty of their life, but became like a crooked bow, and always provoked Him with their idols, on their hills and their mountains; they ate on the mountains, in the forests and among the rocks.

27They slaughtered and sacrificed and rejoiced in the work of their hands, ate what was sacrificed and drank the wine of their drunkenness, and danced and played with demons.

28The demons made all their dancing and play sweet to them, all their drunkenness and fornication without measure, greed and wickedness, in which God does not delight.

29They sacrificed to the carved image of Canaan, to Baal, to Māryā of Midian, to the carved images of the foreigners, Dagon and Apollo, to Artemis and to Rāṣyon,

30and to all the gods of the nations around them. They all worshiped as the nations did, by what they saw and heard, with all the play and dancing and shouting that the nations practice.

31So the people of Israel do, who say, "We worship God," but do not keep His law and His commandment that Moses told them in the Law, to keep the commandments of God and turn away from the worship of idols,

32and not to worship other gods besides the God of their fathers, who fed them the grain of the fields, made them ride on the heights of the earth, satisfied them with honey from the rock and fed them manna.

33He did not withhold from them what they longed for and desired, for He is their God, and He feeds them what they desire.

34But they do not stop provoking God; and when He makes them rejoice, they forget God.

35When He punishes them, they cry out to Him, and He saves them from the distress that found them; and again they rejoice openly and live long days.

36Then at once they turn their hearts and go back to provoking God as of old; and He raises up against them the nations around them, to kill them, make them serve and oppress them.

37Again they turn and rise early and cry out to God their God.

38He too has mercy on them, not for their own sake but for their fathers', with whom He swore and established His covenant, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who pleased God from of old by the beauty of their life.

The Sand and the Stars

39Those who loved Him and kept His commandment He loved, to multiply their seed like the sand of the sea and like the stars of heaven.

40Like the sand of the sea speaks of the souls of the sinners among the sons of Israel, who at the resurrection of the dead go into the sea of fire.

41But the souls of the righteous of the seed of the sons of Israel are like the bright stars above the heavens; for God said to Abraham, "Look at the sky at night and count the stars of heaven, if you can count them." So your seed, the righteous, will shine like the stars in the kingdom of heaven.

42Again He said to him, "Look into the sea and at the bank of the river, and see what is in the sand, and count it, if you can count it." So is your seed that goes down into Sheol at the resurrection of the dead.

43Abraham believed God, and because of this it was counted to him as righteousness. His hope found him on the earth: after his wife Sarah had grown old, she found a son, Isaac.

44Again in the heavens he will find the kingdom because of his faith; for he believed that the dead will rise, and that those who did good will go into eternal life,

45and those who did evil into eternal judgment at the resurrection of the dead; and the righteous who did good will reign with Him forever and ever.

46Those who did evil will be judged forever and ever. Amen and amen.

Notes

  • v4 "son of a slave woman, Ishmaelite" — Hagar's son: Cast out this slave woman with her son (Genesis 21:10); Paul, Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman and one by a free woman (Galatians 4:22).

  • v14 "make them rejoice in My house of prayer… like a sacrifice of offering" — these I will bring to My holy mountain, and make them joyful in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on My altar (Isaiah 56:7).

  • vv21–22 "Abraham My beloved, Isaac My servant, and Jacob in whom My soul delights" — you, Israel, My servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham, My friend (Isaiah 41:8); You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified (Isaiah 49:3).

  • v24 "Their clothes did not wear out… the bread of knowledge" — Your clothing did not wear out on you and your foot did not swell these forty years (Deuteronomy 8:4); she will feed him with the bread of understanding (Sirach 15:3).

  • v26 "like a crooked bow" — they twisted like a deceitful bow (Psalm 78:57). Ṣolāʿət, where they ate, is taken as rocks.

  • v29 the gods — Dagon of the Philistines (12:12), Apollo and Artemis of the Greeks (Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!, Acts 19:28). Māryā of Midian and Rāṣyon are not otherwise known.

  • vv39–42 the sand and the stars — I will surely multiply your offspring as the stars of heaven and as the sand that is on the seashore (Genesis 22:17); Look toward heaven, and number the stars, if you are able to number them… So shall your offspring be (Genesis 15:5). The book reads the two likenesses as the two ends of the resurrection: those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the sky… like the stars forever (Daniel 12:3).

  • v43 "Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness" — Genesis 15:6, quoted by Paul (Romans 4:3) and James (2:23).

  • vv44–46 "those who did good will go into eternal life, and those who did evil into eternal judgment" — those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment (John 5:29). The book ends, as it began (1:15), on the judgment that is forever and ever.

  • Source text — Ge'ez: Beta Masaheft, Universität Hamburg (text of the EOTC printed Bible), CC BY-SA 4.0. English translation by this project.
